items.title: Gov’t to boost waterfront, cultural & eco-tourism in Asuogyaman; area targeted as key destination under $1bn investment drive
items.description: President John Mahama says government intends to position the Asuogyaman District in the Eastern Region as a key destination for waterfront tourism, eco-tourism, cultural heritage, recreation and hospitality investment. He says the move forms part of the government’s tourism and hospitality development agenda under the New Economy Programme, which includes a planned one-billion-dollar investment in the sector. Speaking at the Odwira Akyi Akwasidae celebration and the 15th anniversary of the enstoolment of Odeneho Kwafo Akoto III, President Mahama said Asuogyaman’s natural and cultural attractions remain underutilised despite their potential to generate jobs and improve livelihoods. He identified the Volta River, Lake Volta, the Akosombo landscape, the Adomi Bridge and the historical heritage of Akwamufie as key attractions that could be developed to stimulate economic activity in the area. “Yet we have not fully translated these extraordinary endowments into jobs, incomes, and prosperity for our people. This must change,” he stated. President Mahama said the government wants tourists who visit Akosombo and the Adomi Bridge to spend more time in the area, explore Akwamu’s history and patronise local businesses. He believes this will create economic opportunities for hotels, restaurants, tour guides, transport operators, farmers, artisans and young entrepreneurs. The President also stressed the need to complement tourism investments with improved access roads, clean and attractive public spaces, visitor facilities, safety measures and skills development. He, however, cautioned that the development of tourism attractions must go hand in hand with environmental protection and the preservation of Akwamuman’s cultural heritage. “Our ambition is that when tourists visit Asuogyaman, the benefit must reach the market woman, the fishermen, the farmer, the artisan, and the young entrepreneur,” he said. President Mahama expressed optimism about the area’s prospects, stating that “Akwamuman is poised for progress.”

items.title: El Niño could worsen dust pollution, raise respiratory health risks – GMet
items.description: Expected El Niño conditions early next year could prolong dry spells, worsen dust pollution and increase respiratory health risks in Ghana, the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet) has warned. It said the condition could also reduce rainfall, increase bushfire risks and affect farming, water availability and energy production. The Director-General of the Ghana Meteorological Agency (GMet), Dr Eric Asuman, told the Ghana News Agency that forecasts showed more than 80 per cent confidence that El Niño conditions would persist between January and March. He said prolonged exposure to dusty air could aggravate respiratory and other health conditions, particularly among people with existing illnesses. El Niño, the warm phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), is characterised by unusually warm sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean and can influence weather patterns worldwide. Dr Asuman called on public health authorities to take precautionary measures and intensify public awareness ahead of the expected dry period. He said the forecast, issued in October, had been shared with policymakers, the media and the public to support early planning and preparedness. “The expected conditions are not limited to air quality. Reduced rainfall could also affect farming, increase the risk of bushfires and reduce water availability for energy production,” he said. Dr Asuman warned that bushfires could destroy farms, forests and food supplies, threatening livelihoods and food security. He cited the 1982-1983 bushfires, which destroyed vegetation and food crops and contributed to food shortages, and urged stakeholders to prevent a recurrence. Dr Asuman said the forecast required coordinated preparedness across the health, agriculture, energy, disaster management and national security sectors. He said the Ministry of Food and Agriculture had invited GMet to present the forecast and indicated plans to establish a task force to monitor developments and consider measures to protect farmers. Dr Asuman said the Government had also established an early warning subcommittee, with GMet as a member, to strengthen the use of weather information in disaster preparedness. Under the arrangement, GMet provides hourly forecasts for Accra and issues warnings when projected rainfall exceeds specified thresholds, enabling the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) to send targeted alerts to communities at risk. Dr Asuman also disclosed that installation of a new weather radar purchased for GMet, which had remained in storage for nearly two years, was underway. He said the radar, when operational, would improve the reliability of weather data, forecasts and early warnings, including alerts for heavy rainfall and flooding. Dr Asuman stressed that the forecast did not mean Ghana would experience no rainfall, as some areas could still receive heavy downpours over short periods. He said early preparation was essential to minimise the potential effects of the expected weather conditions on public health, livelihoods and essential services.

items.title: Greater Accra MMDCEs directed to clear, beautify roads ahead of Ghana’s 70th Independence celebrations
items.description: The Greater Accra Regional Minister, Linda Ocloo, has directed all Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) to begin the immediate clearing and beautification of road medians and principal streets across their jurisdictions ahead of Ghana’s 70th Independence anniversary celebrations next year. The directive is part of efforts to improve the appearance and sanitation of the Greater Accra Region in preparation for the national celebration. Addressing a news conference in Accra, Mrs Ocloo instructed the assemblies to remove unauthorised structures, clear pedestrian walkways and restore order along major road corridors. “As the nation’s capital region and the gateway to Ghana, Greater Accra must reflect the pride, dignity and aspirations of our country. “We cannot approach this historic national milestone with public spaces, roads and streets that do not reflect the standards expected of a modern capital region…all Assemblies are directed to immediately commence the clearing, cleaning and beautification of road medians within their respective jurisdictions. Overgrown weeds, refuse, abandoned materials, unauthorised encroachments must be cleared,” she directed. She said the exercise must go beyond major highways to cover principal streets, arterial roads, public spaces and other prominent areas within the various assemblies. She further directed the MMDCEs to undertake landscaping where necessary, including planting ornamental flowers and trees, to give roads and public spaces a “clean and attractive outlook”. Mrs Ocloo said responsibility for the transformation rested with the assemblies, urging them to take immediate action within their respective jurisdictions.

items.title: Bâtie en 11 mois sur fonds propres, l’Académie technologique du Faso officiellement inaugurée par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré
items.description: Le président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a inauguré ce 23 novembre 2026 l’Académie technologique du Faso (ATF) à Pabré, dans la région du Kadiogo. Érigé sur une superficie de 60 hectares et réalisé en 10 mois et 18 jours, ce campus à l’architecture remarquable constitue une étape majeure dans le renforcement des capacités scientifiques et technologiques du pays. Accueillant une première promotion de 241 étudiants, l’ATF est dotée d’amphithéâtres, de salles d’études et de travaux pratiques, de logements étudiants ainsi que d’une cantine universitaire. L’accent est particulièrement mis sur la professionnalisation grâce à des ateliers conçus pour plonger les apprenants dans les conditions réelles de production d’une usine. Présentée comme un projet phare de la Révolution progressiste populaire, l’institution entend répondre aux défis du développement endogène en formant des ingénieurs et techniciens d’excellence alliant culture scientifique, formation humaine et rigueur militaire au service de la nation. L’un des aspects majeurs mis en avant lors de la cérémonie tient au caractère entièrement endogène de l’ouvrage. Selon le Pr Hamidou Sawadogo, Directeur exécutif du Bureau national des grands projets du Burkina Faso (BN-GPB), le chantier a été conduit grâce à l’expertise et à la main-d’œuvre nationales, tout en étant financé sur ressources propres, « sans crédit ». « L’ATF est un complexe architectural qui prouve au monde le génie du peuple burkinabè », a-t-il indiqué. Le président du Faso procède à la coupure du ruban marquant l’ouverture officielle de l’ATF Pour leur part, les étudiants ont exprimé leur gratitude au chef de l’État, soulignant que cette infrastructure, dont la dévise est « Génie, audace, discipline » leur offre l’opportunité de se former sur place plutôt que de s’expatrier. Ils ambitionnent de concevoir des solutions technologiques autonomes et s’engage à préserver le campus. « Devant vous et devant la nation, nous prenons des engagements. Nous prendrons notre formation au sérieux et nous tirerons de ces amphithéâtres et de ces ateliers tout ce qu’ils peuvent nous donner. Nous prendrons soin de nos propres mains de ce campus, car chaque mur porte le sacrifice du contribuable burkinabè », a déclaré Yéri Cynthia Kambou, porte-parole de la première promotion des étudiants de l’ATF. Dans son adresse aux étudiants, le président du Faso a mis en avant l’audace, le génie créateur et la réalisation entièrement burkinabè du projet, affirmant la volonté de valoriser le capital humain et de prouver la capacité du pays à se développer par lui-même. Il les a encouragés à rêver grand sans se fixer de limites, tout en exigeant rigueur et discipline scientifique. Pour le chef de l’État, une souveraineté réelle ne se décrète pas : elle se conquiert par la formation de la ressource humaine, la discipline, l’innovation et la prise de conscience. S’adressant particulièrement aux académiciens de la première promotion, il a insisté sur la nécessité d’un moral d’acier, d’une discipline rigoureuse indispensable au travail scientifique et à la conception, ainsi que d’une capacité à transformer la pression et les défis en moteur de dépassement. Accueillant une première promotion de 241 étudiants, l’ATF est dotée d’amphithéâtres, de salles d’études et de travaux pratiques, de logements étudiants ainsi que d’une cantine universitaire -©Faso7 « Un peuple qui n’est pas audacieux, qui ne développe pas son génie créateur n’a pas d’avenir. Nous avons voulu prouver, à travers la célérité et l’audace de toutes ces infrastructures, ce que nous souhaitons montrer aux yeux du monde : que nous ne sommes pas des sous-hommes, que nous sommes en mesure de prendre soin de notre ressource humaine, de nous projeter et de sortir la tête de l’eau » , a-t-il indiqué. Invitant chacun à l’introspection et à la pleine utilisation de son intelligence au service de la communauté et du réveil de l’Afrique, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré a encouragé les jeunes à ne se fixer aucune limite, qu’il s’agisse de moteurs, de turbopropulseurs, d’équipements biomédicaux ou d’aviation. Il a conclu par un message appelant à la résilience face aux adversités. « Le Burkina Faso est un soleil, un soleil qui brille pour les plus intelligents, qui les éclaire, mais pour ceux-là qui sont nos ennemis ou qui s'érigent en réactionnaires, le soleil ne peut pas les éclairer, ça leur brûle les yeux parce qu'ils forcent de le regarder, ça leur brûle les yeux. ​Nous continuerons d'être ce soleil-là qui brûle les yeux de nos ennemis » , a-t-il déclaré. À noter que la réalisation de cette infrastructure a mobilisé plusieurs acteurs, notamment 11 entreprises nationales, un bureau d’études, trois missions de contrôle, 12 structures techniques publiques, 20 architectes et ingénieurs, 1 435 ouvriers, 65 stagiaires ainsi que plus de 100 activités génératrices de revenus ou petits commerces autour du site, une réussite attribuée à une union sacrée. Lazard KOLA Faso7 L’article Bâtie en 11 mois sur fonds propres, l’Académie technologique du Faso officiellement inaugurée par le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Three Theories of Jensen Huang’s Resurrection
items.description: This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter. Sign up for it here. Eleven days. One Scaramucci. There’s milk in my refrigerator that was bought before Jensen Huang’s downfall, and I may pour a glass to mark his return. To review: Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 after revelations that he’d had an affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy who’d routed embargoed Nvidia chips to Chinese AI companies. Huang allegedly also had an affair with an executive who was one of his 60 direct reports at Nvidia. Five days after the resignation, Nvidia’s board chair, Harvey Jones, said the company “ does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO .” Five days after that, President Trump posted that he hoped it would. This morning, citing “input from senior levels of the United States government,” the board voted unanimously to let him come back. So what’s actually going on in this totally normal corporate-governance situation? Three theories. Theory 1: Money. Nvidia is the engine of the global economy, and without its Leather Daddy CEO, the stock fell about 40 percent from its October peak, losing trillions in value. Following a simple press release announcing his reinstatement, the stock jumped 33 percent, while the overall S&P 500 rose almost 5 percent . Employees wanted him back. Elon Musk signed a petition along with almost 200,000 other people demanding his return. The board—which Huang spent three decades curating, and none of whose members has a history of telling him no—caved to the financial logic. Gatsby returns to the mansion and the AI party roars back to life. Theory 2: Aligned Incentives. The president was briefed about Huang’s involvement with a suspected Chinese spy about a year ago, according to The New York Times . He was briefed again in May, aboard Air Force One, shortly before Huang jumped aboard for a flight to Beijing. Trump brought Huang along anyway. That is … an interesting choice. If you want to speculate about why Trump was (heh) All-In on Jensen , go ahead. But during the 11 days that Huang was a private citizen under investigation by the Justice Department and the Securities and Exchange Commission, he was the most dangerous kind of witness there is. He had no job to protect, no board to answer to, a shattered personal life, and every reason to make his own deal. People in that position tend to tell investigators what they know, about everyone. [ Read: The Jensen Huang scandal should change everything ] Nvidia’s incentives were no better. Under an interim CEO and an independent board, there was nothing to keep the company from opening its files and cooperating. Justice Department policy, historically, rewards that. And a company’s attorney-client privilege is controlled by whoever runs that company. For 11 days, that wasn’t Jensen Huang. But now it is. Huang is back in the room deciding what Nvidia hands over. The general counsel, who sits for an interview with Congress on December 2, reports to him again. And Huang owes his job, at least in part, to the public campaigning of the president. ( Semafor reports that Trump also called into the Nvidia board meeting to lobby members for Huang’s return.) Just like that, Huang, Nvidia, and the White House all want the same thing. That doesn’t necessarily mean Huang will take the Fifth in his December 1 closed-door interview with the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence, and China Select Committees. A sitting CEO who refuses to answer questions is a disaster for his company. In civil cases, silence can be held against him and against the corporation, and the fastest way to wipe out Nvidia’s stock rebound would be for Huang to invoke his right against self-incrimination over and over. Being CEO also makes him the custodian of Nvidia’s records, and under the Supreme Court’s Braswell rule, a person running a company can’t hide behind the Fifth to avoid handing them over. Theory 3: Nothing Matters. A few years ago, every single action in this story would have been a colossal scandal. A CEO resigns over a relationship with a suspected spy. The president, who was reportedly warned about it, campaigns for his return. The board, which said it wouldn’t reinstate him, suddenly reinstates him. To be clear, I suspect that all of this matters quite a bit. But the bet being placed here—by Huang and Trump, by Nvidia’s board, and by the investors pumping up the stock value—is that it doesn’t: that the investigators will wander off, that Congress will take its transcribed interview and move on. Maybe a 33 percent pop settles everything—or maybe executive privilege does. That’s a wild risk. But it’s being taken by people for whom a wild risk may be the last, best strategy left. My glass of milk is just fine. Based on today’s insanity, I suspect they know theirs is spoiled.

items.title: Revisiting the Glossy Fairy Tale of Rocky
items.description: Sign up for Video Village , a new weekly newsletter in which David Sims unearths cinematic gems and brings readers into his movie obsession. Rocky has one of the best corny taglines Hollywood has ever cooked up. “His whole life was a million-to-one shot,” reads the poster ; below it is a stark black-and-white picture of the scrappy boxer Rocky Balboa (played by Sylvester Stallone) holding hands with his beloved Adrian (Talia Shire). Considering now, 50 years after the movie’s release, that this poster was doing its darndest to sell audiences on both a total unknown in Stallone and an outdated genre (the “boxing picture”) is hard. But it worked: Rocky was an out-of-nowhere smash, making more than $200 million globally on a $1 million budget and winning Best Picture at the frankly stacked 1977 Academy Awards. The movie succeeded partly because of how well it packaged that underdog narrative, both on-screen and off. Rocky is about a workaday schlub who is improbably selected for a title bout against the heavyweight champion, Apollo Creed (Carl Weathers). As he goes the distance in the ring, he wins the public’s adoration. But the discussion around the movie quickly coalesced around not its story, but its star. Stallone wrote the film and insisted, despite quite reasonable studio objections over his anonymity, that he play the lead role. His own dreams of triumph are coded into Rocky ’s DNA; it’s a gentle tale about the actor’s hope to make it big in Hollywood, transposed onto a boxer. All of this makes the existence of the new film I Play Rocky all the funnier. Directed by Peter Farrelly and starring the relatively unknown Anthony Ippolito as Stallone, it follows the making of Rocky ; the crux is Stallone’s bullheadedness about, well, playing Rocky. Seriously: The movie’s entire second act seems to involve various studio honchos calling him on the phone to offer more and more implausible amounts of money for him to be only the screenwriter, so that they can install some big star of the era (such as Ryan O’Neal and Burt Reynolds) in the title role instead. The most amusing moments see Tracy Letts as a (fictional) executive growing furious with the back-and-forth, befuddled that this no-name actor would dare turn down hundreds of thousands of dollars to just go away. Funnier still is that I Play Rocky really works, even though it’s basically an adaptation of various Wikipedia articles. The original Rocky already does a fine job exploring Stallone’s striving nature; here, we’re just watching an actor play another actor who’s dreaming big. But Ippolito does a great imitation, and the ensemble, which also includes P. J. Byrne (as the producer Irwin Winkler), Stephan James (as the cocksure Weathers), and Jay Duplass (as Rocky ’s director, John G. Avildsen), provide worthy support. One particularly charming sequence pays loving homage to the Steadicam, a then-recent invention that was used to great effect in Rocky ’s famous museum-steps sequence . The movie, overall, is an easy-to-enjoy ode to moviemaking. To me, though, it mostly illustrates the incredible endurance of the Rocky media brand. The franchise has produced nine entries total (if you include the three Creed films, as you must) and inspired many imitators. Almost every sequel, successful or not, figures out a way to bring our hero back down to earth so that he can be the underdog again: Rocky III acknowledges the character becoming a celebrity, while Rocky IV sees him becoming an anti-Soviet champion fighting on the world stage. Still, each iteration sweats to underline Stallone’s hangdog sweetness and shy, mumbling line delivery. As Stallone became world-famous, his other major franchise, Rambo (introduced in the 1980s once the actor was a cemented star), fully lost sight of what made its title character feel appealing and human, transforming a broken Vietnam veteran into a roided-up, bazooka-toting one-man slaughterhouse. Although the later Rocky movies certainly got cartoonish—the first entry practically feels like an art-house indie in comparison—the hero himself stayed pretty consistent. That’s why Stallone almost won an Oscar for playing the character as a slow-and-steady mentor in Creed 39 years later, and why Ippolito might get his own nod for imitating him. I Play Rocky portrays Stallone as bashful, devoted to his girlfriend and eventual first wife, Sasha (AnnaSophia Robb), and dismissed by everyone around him for seeming to have more brawn than brain. It’s a glossy fairy tale. But then, so is Rocky . An Essay I Enjoyed Lionsgate Hollywood’s Worst Tendencies, in One Movie By Shirley Li Prequels for long-running franchises are tough to pull off. Too many Easter eggs, and the whole project comes across as hollow fan service. Too different from the other installments, and the new entry risks not making sense. But The Hunger Games had a lot of potential to mine new stories from its past. Panem, the totalitarian nation behind the titular battles royal, had a turbulent history filled with cinematic potential, as well as complicated characters whose lives could be further explored. And besides, the original tetralogy, based on Suzanne Collins’s popular YA books, made more than $3 billion at the box office worldwide. Read the full article. Coming Attractions Now expanding in theaters is one of the year’s best debut films—heck, it’s one of the year’s best movies, period. The premise of Jordan Firstman’s Club Kid sounds unbelievably corny, recalling so many ’80s comedies—what if an inveterate party animal in New York’s club scene suddenly found out he was the father of a 10-year-old boy? But Firstman (who wrote, directed, and stars) has a precise sense of place and character, and manages to find a fresh and funny angle on a very schematic-sounding story by observing urban nightlife—and the necessary, healthy ego death that comes with raising a kid. Although Club Kid is mostly about how parenthood changes the adult, rather than the child, it is knowing about that level of self-involvement, and it lands its nuanced, very emotional ending. Also in theaters is La bola negra , a much-hyped epic that made a splashy debut at the Cannes Film Festival in May. It is Netflix’s big hope for the Oscars this year. The movie is a crowd-pleaser with an already vocal fan base, and I admired the scope of the co-directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s vision—yet I was left very frustrated by it. Summarizing everything that’s going on in the triptych of stories is tough, but La bola negra contains: a re-creation of a lost play by the poet Federico García Lorca; a tale of a young man in the Spanish Civil War who becomes a Nationalist in order to survive while nursing his love for a captive Republican soldier; and a section set in the near-present, where a character’s descendant delves into this history and whether it may have, in some way, inspired Lorca. I was most invested in the contemporary storyline and how it explores Spain’s oft-unspoken legacy of fascism. But I felt that the central plot, set in 1937, thematically bit off more than it could chew. Still, given the broad canvas it’s painting on, the movie is worth engaging with on the biggest screen available before it moves to streaming next week. What Else I’m Watching Elsinore is another Oscar contender out now, and it’s worth seeing mostly for Andrew Scott’s lovely work in the lead role. He plays Ian Charleson, the Chariots of Fire actor who died of AIDS at the age of 40—right as he was starring as Hamlet at London’s National Theatre. Scott is tremendous, but the film is otherwise a little sloppily done, relying on formulaic inspirational-movie tropes I thought we’d disposed of long ago. I also caught up with the late Eleanor Coppola’s documentary Making Marie Antoinette , which is streaming on Mubi. It’s in the style of Hearts of Darkness , the film she shot about her husband Francis’s nightmarish time on the set of Apocalypse Now . This is obviously a more sentimental (and calmer) family portrait; Coppola captures her daughter, Sofia, as she works on Marie Antoinette , arguably her best movie. It’s quite sweet and wistful; Coppola (who died in 2024) offers thoughts about her family’s legacy of filmmaking, and the film is charmingly narrated by Diane Lane.

items.title: Le Premier ministre Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô appelle à une « souveraineté partagée » sur les données au service de l’Agenda 2050
items.description: Le Premier ministre, Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô, a officiellement ouvert ce lundi 23 novembre à Dakar le Forum international sur les données (23–25 novembre 2026), placé sous le thème « Gouvernance économique et sociale : la donnée au cœur du développement ». Cette rencontre coïncide avec le vingtième anniversaire de l’Agence nationale de la statistique et de la démographie (ANSD), opérationnelle depuis 2006 après la réforme de 2004. Dans son allocution d'ouverture, le chef du gouvernement a souligné que l'information chiffrée et numérique a changé de statut, passant d'un outil technique à un pilier de l'action publique et de la souveraineté nationale. Il a mis en avant le potentiel transformateur de l'intelligence artificielle, tout en alertant sur les risques associés. « La donnée a cessé d'être l'apanage des seuls techniciens pour devenir un enjeu stratégique de gouvernance, de communication, de souveraineté et de coopération entre les États et entre les institutions. », affirme-t-il. Il poursuit en soulignant que l'intelligence artificielle, qui s'appuie sur ces données ouvre des perspectives de progrès considérables pour nos économies, nos institutions et nos sociétés. Pour autant, le Premier ministre a insisté sur les défis que soulèvent cette révolution numérique : protection de la vie privée, lutte contre la désinformation, prévention des discriminations, cybersécurité et souveraineté numérique. Face à l'abondance d'informations, il a rappelé que la statistique officielle adossée aux principes des Nations unies et à la Charte africaine de la statistique doit demeurer « un bien public de confiance » et « un tiers de vérité ». Gouverner par la preuve à l’horizon Sénégal 2050 Le discours inscrit l'exigence statistique dans la trajectoire de l’Agenda national de transformation, Sénégal 2050. Selon le Premier ministre, une ambition de transformation nationale exige de piloter les politiques publiques sur des faits établis plutôt que sur des approximations ou des intérêts particuliers.« Sans elle, nos décisions risquent de reposer sur des impressions, des intuitions ou des intérêts particuliers. Avec elle, nos choix pourront s'appuyer sur des faits établis, des méthodes rigoureuses et une vision claire de l'avenir », martele-t-il. Il n’a pas manqué d’appeller aux responsables statistiques africains pour mutualiser leurs exigences et bâtir des lignes directrices communes d'accès aux données de masse d'intérêt public, ainsi qu'aux acteurs du numérique pour sceller un cadre équilibré et protecteur des données individuelles avec les États africains, à la poursuite du processus déjà bien avancé afin d'adapter le cadre institutionnel aux réalités actuelles, clarifier le mandat de l'ANSD et renforcer la coordination du Système statistique national et des services sectoriels, à la mise en avant du principe retenu par le gouvernement pour créer un fonds alimenté par l'État et ouvert aux partenaires, afin d'éviter la dépendance aux financements ponctuels et intermittents pour les recensements et enquêtes et à dépasser le simple diagnostic pour produire des recommandations et engagements concrets sur des sujets allant du financement et de la souveraineté statistique à la place des femmes dans les données, l'interopérabilité, les sources géospatiales et mobiles, le climat, l'agriculture ou le pari démographique. items.title: 'No national security risk': Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after affair scandal
items.description: Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior US government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal. The board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candour and ability to lead,” the company said in a statement. Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board. Nvidia shares surged on the news, jumping more than 25 per cent in premarket trading. The decision came three days after US President Donald Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance”. Trump described Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions,” and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart.” Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused. Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.” Huang, 63, stepped down on Nov 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia. US intelligence services reportedly concluded she passed information to Beijing, which has denied the allegations. Board chair Harvey Jones said Monday that directors now believe Huang “is the right person to lead Nvidia” and that his return serves the interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers. Jones, a former Synopsys chief executive who was named Nvidia’s first-ever board chair during the crisis, will stay in the role. Chief financial officer Colette Kress , who served as interim CEO, will continue as CFO. Nvidia said a committee of independent directors set up earlier this month to investigate whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort will see its probe through to the end. Huang supports the investigation and has committed to cooperating, the company said. Trump, who had previously called on the AI giant to reinstate Huang, congratulated him in a post on Truth Social. “The Nvidia board of directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO. The country needs Jensen’s leadership at Nvidia in order to ensure the success and prosperity of not only the company, but the American economy,” he wrote. The US president clarified that the US government had “no reason” to believe that Huang’s reinstatement posed risks to national security, adding that the US attorney general had confirmed that the government did not possess evidence against Huang. Trump further said that he had gotten to know Huang, describing him as a “great patriot and national treasure”. Trump directed that Nvidia should continue its internal investigation into compliance with US export controls. Trump told CNBC on Monday that Huang “didn’t know about” advanced Nvidia chips going to China. The US president described him as a “ genius ” and a “ brilliant guy ”, adding: “Losing the brainpower of somebody like Jensen — to me, that would be a far bigger threat than anything we’re talking about.“ “As far as the woman is concerned, every time you have a Chinese woman that’s good-looking or beautiful, they say she’s a spy. Now with Swalwell, she probably was a spy — but with Jensen, I don’t believe that’s true,” Trump said. Jack Gold of J. Gold Associates called the reinstatement “a big mistake”, noting that the investigation into whether Huang was compromised by the alleged spy was still under way. “This action further amplifies the notion that big ‘tech bros’ don’t need to play by the rules like the rest of us do,” Gold said, adding that the board’s decision appeared “driven more by financial influences than ethical practices”. US Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer vowed to investigate potential wrongdoing surrounding Huang’s reinstatement, accusing Trump of putting personal financial interests ahead of national security. “Democrats will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other Nvidia executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain,” said the veteran New Yorker, who is seen as likely to remain in his position when Democrats take control of Congress in January. Alice Huang had contact with China spy agency: NYT Alice Huang, the alleged spy at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, was in touch with an official from China’s top spy agency during an affair with the chip giant’s former chief executive, the New York Times reported on Sunday. She was in contact with an officer of China’s Ministry of State Security from the spring of 2025 until the fall of this year, the Times reported, citing people with knowledge of the intelligence. According to the Times , Alice Huang’s contacts with the Chinese spy agency correspond to the affair as well as a period when Megaspeed was acquiring large amounts of advanced Nvidia chips. The Times also reported that US intelligence agencies have gathered evidence that Alice Huang’s business partner Kang Wei — who the newspaper said was often introduced as her husband — worked with the same Chinese spy agency. He is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns.

items.title: Gender Ministry to lead Ghana’s 2026 16 Days of Activism against gender-based violence
items.description: The Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection will lead Ghana’s observance of the 2026 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence from November 25 to December 10, with a focus on improving access to justice for survivors and ending impunity for perpetrators. The campaign will be held under the global theme, “ UNITE to End Violence Against Women and Girls: Ensure Justice, Protect Survivors, End Impunity.” The annual campaign runs from the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on November 25 to Human Rights Day on December 10, highlighting violence against women and girls as a violation of human rights rather than a private family matter. The Ministry said the campaign remained necessary despite progress made in addressing gender-based violence, as the problem continued to affect women and girls in homes, communities, schools, workplaces and increasingly in online spaces. Citing the 2022 Ghana Demographic and Health Survey, the Ministry said 41.6 per cent of women aged 15 to 49 had experienced emotional, physical or sexual violence from an intimate partner. It added that one in three women had experienced physical violence since the age of 15, while more than one in ten had experienced sexual violence from an intimate partner. The survey also found that 16 per cent of young women aged 20 to 24 had been married before turning 18, with domestic violence affecting more than six in ten women in some districts. The Minister for Gender, Children and Social Protection, Dr Agnes Naa Momo Lartey, said the figures represented the experiences of women and girls whose access to protection and justice needed to be strengthened. “Behind every one of these numbers is a mother, a daughter, a sister or a friend,” she said. “Our laws are strong, but a law only protects a woman if she knows about it, can use it, and sees it enforced. Too many survivors who find the courage to report never get justice, and too many perpetrators face no consequences. This must change.” The Ministry also raised concerns about the growing use of digital platforms to perpetrate violence against women, particularly the non-consensual recording and circulation of intimate images. It reminded the public that sharing such images, or threatening to share them, constitutes an offence under the Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038), adding that people who forward the images could also face legal consequences. The campaign will therefore seek to address the gap between reporting cases of abuse and securing justice for survivors, both online and offline. The Ministry said it was working with partners to organise activities at the national, regional and community levels to raise public awareness, improve support for survivors and strengthen access to justice. The activities will also coincide with the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage on November 27, World AIDS Day on December 1, the International Day of Persons with Disabilities on December 3 and Human Rights Day on December 10. The Ministry said the observances highlighted the particular vulnerabilities of girls at risk of child marriage, women living with HIV and women with disabilities, stressing the need to ensure that no one was left behind. It called on chiefs, queen mothers and religious leaders to use their influence to condemn violence and encourage survivors to report abuse. Parents and families were also urged not to conceal abuse to protect family reputations but rather to prioritise the safety and protection of women and children. Young people were cautioned against sharing, forwarding or downloading private images of others and encouraged to speak up when they witnessed abuse. Men and boys were also invited to support efforts to end violence against women and girls. The Ministry further urged employers to provide safe workplaces and support staff affected by violence, while calling on the media to help spread the campaign’s messages and report cases in ways that protect survivors. Members of the public are encouraged to wear orange throughout the 16-day campaign and share its messages using the hashtags #16Days, #OrangeGhana and #EndImpunityGH. People experiencing violence, or those who know someone affected, are encouraged to report to the Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU) of the Ghana Police Service, the nearest police station or a Department of Social Welfare office. Dr Lartey said every woman and girl in Ghana deserved to live free from violence and fear. “Together, we can ensure justice, protect survivors and end impunity,” she added, while wishing Ghanaians a safe and peaceful festive season. items.title: BECE directive must make room for exceptionally talented pupils – NCPTA
items.description: The National Council of Parent-Teacher Associations (NCPTA) has called on education authorities to make room for exceptionally gifted pupils under the directive restricting students from writing the Basic Education Certificate Examination (BECE) ahead of the prescribed school progression. The General Secretary of the NCPTA, Raphael Kofi Gapson, says while the directive is necessary to prevent parents and schools from deliberately pushing children into examinations before they are adequately prepared, exceptions should be made for pupils who demonstrate exceptional academic ability. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Monday, November 23, he said enforcing the directive without considering exceptional cases could waste the time and potential of gifted children. He said some pupils are capable of grasping concepts, demonstrating literacy and numeracy skills, and applying critical thinking at a level beyond their age group. “So we are saying that this directive is good, but in situations where genuinely there are students who are exceptionally talented, there should always be a caveat where there is genuine justification for the child to progress,” he said. Mr Gapson argued that making such children wait until they meet the standard progression timeline could amount to a waste of both their time and state resources. He explained that Ghana’s basic education structure provides for two years of kindergarten, six years of primary education and three years of junior high school before pupils sit for the BECE. However, he maintained that pupils who can demonstrate the ability to compete academically with learners in higher grades should be considered for early progression. He stressed that the proposed exemptions should apply only where there is clear justification, warning against situations where parents or schools deliberately advance children who are not adequately prepared for the examination. “Where they deliberately jump the child, but the child is not adequately prepared to go and write the BECE, I think that we should allow the status quo to remain,” he added.

items.title: Give deserving prisoners sentence cuts for Christmas – Annoh-Dompreh urges Mahama
items.description: Minority Chief Whip Frank Annoh-Dompreh has appealed to President John Mahama to consider reducing the sentences of deserving inmates as a Christmas gesture to help ease overcrowding in Ghana’s prisons. The Nsawam-Adoagyiri MP made the call during a visit to the Nsawam Medium Security Prisons, where he donated food and essential supplies to support inmates. He said sentence remission could provide immediate relief while the government pursued longer-term measures to address congestion and improve prison conditions. For example, he suggested that some inmates serving 10-year sentences could have their terms reduced to five years, subject to necessary legal and administrative considerations. Annoh-Dompreh said his repeated visits had shown him the difficulties inmates and prison authorities face. He recalled being particularly disturbed by overcrowding during an earlier visit. While donations could help meet immediate needs, he argued that they could not replace government action on inadequate facilities and congestion. The MP also called for greater use of alternative sentencing for appropriate offences. He said imprisonment should not automatically be the preferred punishment where lawful alternatives were available. He said he would pursue the issue in Parliament and push the Interior Minister to explain the government’s plans to reduce overcrowding. Annoh-Dompreh also sought an update on a prison facility initiated under the previous New Patriotic Party administration. He said the project was nearly complete and intended to ease congestion. He urged the minister to outline the status of the facility and broader plans to improve prison infrastructure. During the visit, the MP presented 36 bags of beans, 34 bags of maize, boxes of soup, detergents and other essential items. He valued the donation at approximately US$60,000 and said he hoped to make another contribution in the first quarter of next year. Annoh-Dompreh commended prison authorities for putting previous donations to good use. He also encouraged individuals and organisations to support inmates, saying their welfare was a shared responsibility. He urged the public to recognise that prisoners remained part of society and should not be forgotten. Receiving the items, the Eastern Regional Commander and Officer in Charge of the Nsawam Medium Security Prisons, Deputy Director of Prisons Patrick Thomas Seidu, thanked the MP for his continued support. He described the donation as helpful to prison management and encouraged other individuals and organisations to contribute to inmates’ welfare.

items.title: Fire safety critical to success of 24-hour economy – Chief Fire Officer
items.description: The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) has urged businesses and industries to strengthen fire prevention measures to protect investments and support Ghana’s proposed 24-hour economy. The Service said effective emergency preparedness and compliance with fire safety regulations would be critical to sustaining extended business operations and economic growth. The Chief Fire Officer, Daniella Mawusi Ntow-Sapong, made the call at the launch of the 2026 Annual Fire Safety Week celebration in Accra. It was on the theme: “ Prevent Fires, Protect Productivity: Ghana National Fire Service and Stakeholders Building a Safe 24-hour Economy. ” The celebration, scheduled for November 23 to 27, is aimed at promoting public awareness, strengthening stakeholder collaboration, and encouraging practical fire prevention measures. Mrs. Ntow-Sapong said the proposed 24-hour economy presented opportunities for increased productivity, job creation, business expansion and national development, but those gains could only be sustained if the safety of workers, businesses, public facilities and communities was assured. She said fire outbreaks could destroy investments, disrupt business activities, threaten jobs, and undermine economic growth. Mrs. Ntow-Sapong urged businesses and organisations to ensure that firefighting equipment was available and properly maintained. She said workers must receive regular fire safety training, while electrical installations and other fire hazards should be inspected routinely. The Chief Fire Officer urged establishments operating around the clock to pay particular attention to emergency communication systems, evacuation procedures, and the availability of trained personnel. She also called on Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) to strengthen collaboration with the GNFS in building inspections, development planning, public education and enforcement of fire safety requirements. The Deputy Minister for the Interior and Member of Parliament for Lower Manya Krobo, Ebenezer Okletey Terlabi, said fire safety must form an integral part of Ghana’s economic transformation agenda. He said longer operating hours required stronger emergency preparedness, effective fire prevention systems, and responsible business practices. “A 24-hour economy must also be a safe economy,” he said. Mr. Terlabi said markets, factories, warehouses, hotels, hospitals, fuel stations, transport terminals and other commercial establishments must have appropriate fire prevention and emergency response measures. He noted that a single fire outbreak could destroy businesses, displace workers, disrupt essential services, and cause significant financial losses, with the potential to undermine investor confidence. The Deputy Minister assured the GNFS of the Government’s commitment to improving the Service’s operational capacity through modern equipment, professional development and enhanced staff welfare. He said the Government remained committed to retooling the security and emergency services, including the GNFS, with modern fire tenders, rescue equipment, protective gear and other operational assets. Mr. Terlabi said the success of fire safety interventions should be measured not only by the equipment provided but also by lives saved, fires contained, emergencies effectively managed and property protected. He highlighted the introduction of the Automated Fire Safety Compliance System (AFCAS), an initiative aimed at modernising fire safety administration in the country. Mr. Terlabi said the digital platform was designed to improve certification, compliance monitoring, and public engagement by replacing manual procedures with a more efficient and transparent system. He said AFCAS would support a shift from reactive emergency response to proactive fire risk management, prevention and accountability. The Deputy Minister encouraged businesses, institutions and property owners to embrace the system and ensure their premises were assessed, certified and equipped in line with fire safety regulations. He also condemned attacks on firefighters and obstruction of emergency operations, describing such actions as unacceptable and a threat to public safety. Mr. Terlabi urged the public to cooperate with firefighters, provide access to emergency scenes, and refrain from interfering with their work. He commended officers of the GNFS for their dedication and sacrifices and urged stakeholders to strengthen collaboration with the Service to build safer workplaces, businesses and communities.

items.title: Two arrested over alleged sexual extortion in Accra, face up to 25 years in prison
items.description: The Cyber Security Authority (CSA), working with other security agencies, has arrested two 22-year-old men in separate cases of alleged sexual extortion involving a teenage girl and an estranged girlfriend in Accra. In a statement issued on November 19, 2026, the Authority said the first suspect, a law student, was arrested on November 13 over allegations that he blackmailed a 16-year-old female senior high school student using intimate images. According to the CSA, the victim met the suspect on Snapchat about a year ago. During their conversations, he allegedly requested nude images from her in exchange for money. The Authority said the victim subsequently sent the images, which the suspect allegedly used to threaten her, demanding money and warning that he would publish the videos on social media if she failed to pay. In a separate incident, another 22-year-old man, identified as a National Service Personnel, was arrested on November 15 in connection with the alleged extortion of his 18-year-old estranged girlfriend. The CSA said the suspect had allegedly recorded sessions of sexual intercourse between them and used the videos to blackmail the woman into continuing the relationship or risk having the recordings published online. Both suspects face charges of sexual extortion under Section 66(2) of the Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038), which provides for a prison term of between 10 and 25 years upon conviction. Section 66 of the Cybersecurity Act criminalises threats to distribute or transmit intimate images of another person or a child engaged in sexually explicit conduct, where the threat is made with the specific intention of harassing, threatening, coercing, intimidating or exerting undue influence on the person. The provision also covers threats intended to extort money or other consideration or compel a victim to engage in unwanted sexual activity. A person found guilty under the provision is liable, on summary conviction, to imprisonment for not less than 10 years and not more than 25 years. The Act also addresses the production and possession of indecent images of children. Section 62 provides for prison terms of between five and 10 years upon conviction. The Authority has urged the public, particularly young people, to exercise caution when interacting with strangers online and avoid taking or sharing intimate photographs and videos. It encouraged people to report suspected cases of online sexual exploitation and abuse through its call or text line, 292, or by email at report@csa.gov.gh . The CSA said the arrests were carried out in collaboration with other security agencies.

items.title: Emergency Room: Inside the EU-UK reset deal
items.description: In today’s Emergency Room episode, Mark Leonard welcomes Jannike Wachowiak , head of strategy for ECFR’s EU-UK project. Together they discuss British prime minister Andy Burnham’s meeting with European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen and European Council president António Costa at the second EU-UK summit, and what it means for the relationship. Jannike decodes the deals on agri-food trade, emissions trading and a youth experience scheme, which mark the first time since Brexit that Britain has agreed to dynamic alignment with EU law in limited areas. She discusses why tuition fees and the “Made in Europe” scheme ended up linked, and whether the reaction was overblown—and explains why the summit marks the start of a more political, less technocratic, phase. How far can cooperation on defence and migration go without treaty change? Can Brussels and London run a genuine brainstorming exercise on the future relationship? items.title: Beyla : le MATD dément une prétendue crise humanitaire après la fermeture des sites d’orpaillage
items.description: Le ministère de l’Administration du territoire et de la Décentralisation (MATD) a formellement démenti les informations relayées sur les réseaux sociaux faisant état d’une prétendue crise humanitaire dans certaines localités de la région de Beyla, à la suite de la fermeture des sites d’exploitation artisanale de l’or. Dans un communiqué publié le 20 novembre 2026, le département dirigé par Madame Camara Djenabou Touré réagit à une vidéo largement diffusée sur les réseaux sociaux. Celle-ci évoque des centaines de personnes privées de nourriture, d’eau potable et de logement, contraintes de dormir à la belle étoile ou de trouver refuge dans des lieux de culte. La vidéo fait également état d’une prétendue alerte de la Croix-Rouge appelant à une intervention urgente. Face à ces allégations, le MATD oppose un démenti formel et dénonce une présentation qu’il juge alarmiste. Le ministère estime que de telles informations ne peuvent être considérées comme des faits établis sans vérification préalable auprès des autorités compétentes. Le département rappelle que les mesures gouvernementales relatives à la réglementation et à la sécurisation des activités minières visent notamment la préservation de l’ordre public, la protection des populations et la défense de l’environnement. Dans son communiqué, le ministère met également en demeure les auteurs, initiateurs et diffuseurs des informations concernées de procéder à une rectification publique et de présenter des excuses dans les mêmes espaces de diffusion, avec une visibilité équivalente. À défaut, le MATD annonce se réserver le droit de saisir les autorités judiciaires compétentes afin que les responsabilités soient établies et que les sanctions prévues par les lois en vigueur soient appliquées. Le ministère invite enfin les citoyens à privilégier les sources officielles et à faire preuve de discernement face aux contenus diffusés sur les réseaux sociaux. items.title: Burkina Faso : Touobawènèkaon Maximin Somda décroche son doctorat avec les félicitations du jury sur la protection du corridor forestier de la Boucle du Mouhoun
items.description: La thèse de doctorat unique de Touobawènèkaon Maximin Somda, consacrée au thème « Corridor forestier de la Boucle du Mouhoun : analyse socio-anthropologique des conditions de protection par les populations riveraines de deux villages du Nayala (Konrombèrè et Tani, Burkina Faso) », a été reçue à l’unanimité par les membres du jury, à l’issue de sa soutenance tenue le samedi 21 novembre 2026 à l’Université Nazi Boni (UNB) de Bobo-Dioulasso. Les travaux ont été examinés sous la présidence du professeur titulaire Amadou Oumarou, de l’Université Abdou Moumouni (UAM) du Niger. C’est la mention « très honorable » qui a été décernée par l’ensemble du jury au travail de recherche de l’impétrant, inscrit à l’École doctorale Sciences naturelles et agronomie de l’Université Nazi Boni. À l’issue de sa présentation, des observations et de ses éléments de réponse, Touobawènèkaon Maximin Somda accède désormais au grade de docteur. Le jury, présidé par le professeur titulaire Amadou Oumarou de l’UAM du Niger, était également composé de Jérôme Yaméogo, maître de conférences à l’Université Nazi Boni (rapporteur), de Ludovic Kibora, directeur de recherche au CNRST de Ouagadougou (rapporteur), et de Clotaire Alexis Bassolé, professeur titulaire à l’Université Joseph Ki-Zerbo (examinateur), aux côtés du directeur de thèse, le professeur Patrice Toé. À l’issue de ses recherches, le Dr Touobawènèkaon Maximin Somda explique que son sujet est né d’un constat alarmant sur le terrain : « Nous avons constaté une dégradation des ressources forestières dans les deux villages de l'étude, à savoir Konrombèrè et Tani, dans la province du Nayala. Cette dégradation entraîne un ensablement du fleuve Mouhoun. C'est l'ensemble de ces constats qui nous ont conduit à analyser, d'un point de vue socio-anthropologique, les conditions dans lesquelles les populations acceptent de protéger l'environnement », a-t-il confié. Conduire cette étude n’a toutefois pas été un long fleuve tranquille en raison du contexte sécuritaire difficile. « C'est un soulagement et une joie pour nous, parce qu'on avait perdu confiance et on se demandait si cela allait aboutir vu les contraintes croisées sur le terrain. Les deux villages étaient marqués par la présence de groupes terroristes et, à plusieurs reprises, l'accès nous a été interdit. Nous avons dû adopter une autre méthode pour terminer l'étude, mais aujourd'hui, c'est une vraie joie d'être parvenu au bout » , s’est réjoui le nouveau docteur. Un aboutissement salué par son directeur de thèse, le professeur titulaire Patrice Toé, qui n’a pas tari d’éloges sur la qualité scientifique et pratique du document : « L'impétrant a fait un bon travail et le jury est unanime. Le travail est d'une très belle facture sur le plan scientifique. Je crois que les résultats auxquels il est parvenu sont directement utilisables par les autorités publiques et, en même temps, très utiles pour les populations locales » , a-t-il conclu. Faso7 L’article Burkina Faso : Touobawènèkaon Maximin Somda décroche son doctorat avec les félicitations du jury sur la protection du corridor forestier de la Boucle du Mouhoun est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Koudougou: le Lallé Naaba démet le chef du quartier Bourkina de ses fonctions
items.description: La cour royale du Lallé a annoncé, ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, la destitution de Naaba Baongho, chef du quartier Bourkina de Koudougou. A en croire l’Agence d’information du Burkina qui a relayé cette information, la décision est motivée par des faits de «défaut d'allégeance et manquements aux usages coutumiers», notamment son attitude lors de l'ouverture des Nuits atypiques de Koudougou (NAK), le samedi 21 novembre dernier. La décision est tombée. Sa Majesté le Lallé Naaba Guigmdé a retiré à Naaba Baongho son titre de chef du quartier Bourkina de Koudougou. L'annonce a été faite, ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, par la cour royale du Lallé, qui lui reproche plusieurs manquements aux obligations coutumières et à l'autorité traditionnelle. Les raisons de cette destitution ont été détaillées lors d'un point de presse organisé au palais royal. Plusieurs dignitaires de la cour, dont le prince Sidiki Kaboré, le Ouid-Nabiga Mathias Ouédraogo, le Ouidi-Naaba Baongo, le Tensoaba Bilga et le Malgré Naaba Tanga, ont pris part à cette rencontre. Leurs déclarations ont été traduites en français par Barthélemy Gamsonré, également membre de la cour. Parmi les griefs formulés contre l'ancien chef figure son éloignement progressif du palais royal. D'après les explications de Barthélemy Gamsonré, Naaba Baongho aurait commencé à ne plus fréquenter la cour à partir de 2012. Il lui est également reproché de n'avoir pas accompli les formalités coutumières d'allégeance auprès du Lallé Naaba Guigmdé, depuis l'intronisation de ce dernier en 2021. La cour lui impute, par ailleurs, des attitudes considérées comme contraires aux traditions lors de certaines cérémonies organisées dans le quartier Bourkina. Il aurait notamment tenu des propos désobligeants à l'égard d'émissaires du Lallé Naaba. Mais l'épisode qui aurait précipité cette décision remonte à l'ouverture de la 29e édition des Nuits atypiques de Koudougou. Selon la version présentée par la cour royale, lors du passage du Lallé Naaba sur le site du festival, Édouard Yaméogo ne se serait pas plié aux marques de déférence coutumière observées par les autres chefs présents. Il n'aurait pas non plus manifesté publiquement son allégeance à l'autorité traditionnelle. Au regard de l'ensemble de ces reproches, le Lallé Naaba Guigmdé a prononcé la destitution de Naaba Baongho. La sanction concerne également, selon les dignitaires, les responsables coutumiers que celui-ci avait lui-même intronisés à ses côtés. La procédure ayant conduit à cette décision aurait été enclenchée dès le dimanche 22 novembre 2026, avec l'implication des chefs de terre des cinq grands quartiers de Koudougou. Désormais, la cour royale entend porter officiellement cette décision à la connaissance des autorités administratives, afin que les mesures appropriées soient prises pour tenir compte de cette destitution. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Koudougou: le Lallé Naaba démet le chef du quartier Bourkina de ses fonctions est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Daily Insight for CEOs: The CEO’s role in strengthening organisational culture
items.description: Insight. Organisational culture is one of the most powerful influences on business performance. It shapes how people work, make decisions, treat customers, manage conflict and respond to challenges. While culture develops through everyday interactions, the CEO plays a decisive role in defining the standards and behaviours that become accepted across the organisation. A strong culture does not happen by chance. It requires clarity about organisational values, consistency in leadership conduct and deliberate reinforcement of the behaviours that support strategic priorities. Employees pay attention to what leader’s reward, what they tolerate and what they hold people accountable for. As the year approaches its end, CEOs must assess whether the organization’s culture is supporting the performance, innovation and accountability required for 2027. Culture must become a practical driver of results, not simply a statement displayed on office walls. Key Strategies: Define the desired culture: Establish clear values and behaviours that support the organisation’s vision and strategic direction. Lead by example: Ensure that executive conduct reflects the standards expected throughout the organisation. Align culture with performance: Recognise and reward behaviours that promote collaboration, ownership, innovation and results. Address cultural barriers: Identify practices, attitudes and leadership behaviours that undermine organisational effectiveness. Measure cultural progress: Use employee feedback, engagement indicators and performance reviews to assess cultural health. CEO Leadership Actions. Review whether the organisation’s stated values are reflected in actual workplace behaviours and management decisions. Engage employees and managers to identify cultural strengths and areas requiring improvement. Hold the executive team accountable for demonstrating and reinforcing the desired organisational culture. Actionable Tip. Identify three behaviours that must become more visible across your organisation in 2027. Communicate them clearly and ensure that every executive demonstrates them consistently. Why This Matters? A healthy organisational culture improves employee engagement, strengthens collaboration, and creates an environment where people take responsibility for results. It also supports innovation, customer service, and organisational resilience. The culture a CEO builds today will influence the organisation’s performance long after the CEO has left office. About the Author. Ernest De-Graft Egyir, CEO advisor, Thought Leader and Founding CEO of Chief Executives Network Ghana, convenes the Ghana CEO Summit and served on Ghana’s Economic Dialogue Planning Committee.

items.title: GNCCI urges government to deepen private sector engagement in New Economy Agenda
items.description: The Ghana National Chamber of Commerce and Industry (GNCCI) has urged the government to deepen its engagement with the private sector in implementing its New Economy Agenda, insisting businesses must play a central role in shaping economic reforms, job creation and growth. The Chamber says closer collaboration with businesses will be critical to translating government’s economic vision into tangible results, particularly as the country seeks to consolidate macroeconomic stability and improve the operating environment for businesses. Speaking at the Chamber’s 6th Awards ceremony, President of the GNCCI, Nana Agyenim Boateng, called on government to open up further consultations with the private sector and draw on the Chamber’s expertise in developing and executing its economic policies. His remarks come following the launch of government’s New Economy Agenda and the presentation of the 2027 Budget, which outlines reforms aimed at reducing the cost of doing business, improving access to financing and strengthening economic productivity. The Chamber believes stronger private sector participation will be essential to expanding businesses, creating sustainable jobs and accelerating the country’s economic transformation. Meanwhile, Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has urged businesses to embrace technology, sustainability and skills development to remain competitive in an evolving global economy. She says businesses must position themselves to take advantage of emerging opportunities while adapting to changing market demands and the growing importance of innovation. The 2026 GNCCI Awards also recognised outstanding contributions across various sectors, including the media. Multimedia Group’s Pious Kojo Backah received the Media Personality Award for his contribution to journalism and media practice. The Chamber says although recent macroeconomic stability has improved business confidence and planning, sustained collaboration between government and industry remains crucial to achieving the objectives of the 24-hour economy and building a resilient, productive private sector.

items.title: Le secrétaire général de l'OTAN imagine Poutine à Rotterdam et appelle l’Europe à s’armer contre la Russie
items.description: Il suffirait de deux ou trois semaines de discussions europeennes pour que Vladimir Poutine arrive a Rotterdam. C'est le scenario avance par Mark Rutte le 23 novembre, a Berlin, devant l'Assemblee parlementaire de l'OTAN. Non pour annoncer une attaque imminente, mais pour expliquer pourquoi il ne veut pas d'une armee europeenne independante de l'Alliance. Rotterdam avant la fin des reunions ? Le secretaire general de l'OTAN a declare : « Je deconseillerais de creer une grande structure militaire europeenne venant se superposer aux forces armees nationales, qui cooperent deja au sein de l'OTAN. Parce que dans ce cas, si Poutine nous attaque, il nous faudra d'abord deux ou trois semaines pour nous mettre d'accord sur qui fait quoi. Et le temps qu'on se decide, il sera probablement deja a Rotterdam. C'est la tout mon argument. Je n'ai donc pas d'objection de principe a la creation d'une armee europeenne. Mais, je le repete, je ne la vois pas se concretiser de sitot. Je ne crois pas qu'il y ait de reelle volonte de la creer. » Rutte imagine les blocages politiques d'un commandement parallele. L'Alliance possede deja sa propre chaîne de commandement : le message est donc moins de bâtir une nouvelle force que de renforcer celle qui existe. Difficile, toutefois, de ne pas comparer cette mise en scene avec ses propos du 30 septembre. Interroge par Euronews, Rutte assurait alors qu'aucune menace immediate ne pesait sur le territoire de l'OTAN. Moins de deux mois apres, Rotterdam devient le decor d'une offensive russe hypothetique. La fin du conflit ? Pas celle du rearmement Le meme jour, Rutte a reconnu la puissance de l'industrie militaire russe : « Nous savons que la machine de guerre russe tourne aujourd'hui a plein regime. L'economie de guerre de la Russie continue de se developper. Elle ne s'arretera pas lorsque la guerre contre l'Ukraine prendra fin un jour, comme nous l'esperons. Toute cette machine est deja en place et elle continuera de tourner. » Autrement dit, meme une cessation des combats en Ukraine ne modifierait pas, a ses yeux, la necessite d'un rearmement durable. Les membres de l'Alliance ont decide, au sommet de La Haye en juin 2025, de porter leurs depenses de defense et depenses associees a 5 % du PIB d'ici 2035. L'argument russe sert ainsi a defendre des budgets qui continueront de croître bien apres une eventuelle paix. Moscou tient un discours oppose. Le 25 septembre, Vladimir Poutine a declare que la Russie ne preparait aucune operation militaire contre les etats europeens. Le 1er octobre, il a de nouveau rejete l'idee d'une attaque, tout en prevenant qu'une agression contre la Russie provoquerait une riposte. Cette distinction entre attaque et reponse est absente du scenario presente a Berlin. Une coalition europeenne qui peine a faire l'unanimite Les projets militaires se multiplient pourtant en Europe. Reunis a Berlin le 19 novembre, les dirigeants francais, allemand, britannique et ukrainien ont evoque une force multinationale dirigee par des Europeens et soutenue par les etats-Unis, susceptible d'etre deployee apres un cessez-le-feu en Ukraine. Il ne s'agirait pas d'une armee de l'Union europeenne, mais d'une coalition de pays volontaires. L'unite affichee connaît deja ses limites. La Pologne a refuse d'envoyer des soldats en Ukraine , malgre les projets de la coalition. De son cote, Emmanuel Macron souhaite relancer le debat sur une adhesion de Kiev a l'OTAN , une perspective fermement rejetee par Moscou. Pour Moscou, le deploiement de troupes europeennes en Ukraine ne constituerait pas une simple garantie de securite. Le 17 novembre, lors d'une conference de presse a Manille, le ministre russe des Affaires etrangeres, Sergueï Lavrov, a mis en garde les pays concernes : « Pourquoi veulent-ils une treve ? Pour y deployer aussitot des forces de stabilisation. On les a prevenus mille fois. Le president l'a dit. Votre humble serviteur aussi, et beaucoup d'autres responsables : tout deploiement de forces de stabilisation signifiera, de maniere indiscutable, que l'Europe entre directement en guerre. »

items.title: Démarrage des travaux de construction de la cité ministérielle : L’ordre de service officiellement remis à la société exécutante
items.description: Lomé, 23 nov. (ATOP) – La directrice de cabinet du ministre des Finances et du Budget, Mawussé Adetou Afidenyigba a remis officiellement l’ordre de service marquant le démarrage des travaux de construction de la cité ministérielle au représentant de la Société de construction de la cité ministérielle (SOCO CIM), Tarzaali Fabrice, le lundi 23 novembre à Lomé. M. Tarzaali dont la société représente l’Etat dans le cadre de la construction de cette cité a retransmis l’ordre de service à Zadi Luc, directeur Pôle Bâtiment, de la société PFO Construction, chargé de l’exécution de la construction de la cité ministérielle. Cette remise de l’ordre de service marque le point de départ effectif du projet dont la réussite repose sur l’engagement, la rigueur et le sens des responsabilités de toutes les parties prenantes. Pour la directrice de cabinet, la construction de cette cité répond à une nécessité stratégique, en l’occurrence celle de doter l’administration togolaise d’infrastructures plus modernes, fonctionnelles et adaptées aux exigences d’une gouvernance publique plus performante. « La concentration des services ministériels dans un cadre institutionnel approprié permettra de renforcer la coordination entre les départements ministériels, de faciliter la collaboration administrative, d’améliorer l’accueil et les services rendus aux usagers, tout en favorisant une meilleure utilisation des ressources publiques », a fait comprendre Mme Afidenyigba. Selon M. Tarzaali, toutes les conditions sont aujourd’hui réunies, que ce soit au niveau environnemental, administratif et financier, pour la réussite de ce projet. « Je suis très rassuré de délivrer cet ordre de service à l’entreprise PFO Construction. J’ai confiance dans le démarrage, dans le lancement, et dans les relations établies entre l’entreprise, le contrôle et l’administration, pour que ce soit une réussite », a indiqué M. Tarzaali. L’opération de construction de cette cité ministérielle a été organisée en deux phases. La première phase, concerne la construction de quatre tours administratives dont deux rez-de-chaussée plus treize étages et deux rez-de-chaussée plus huit étages ; la réalisation de deux tours bas de rez-de-chaussée plus trois étages. Il est prévu également la construction d’un mur d’enceinte du site d’un peu moins d’un kilomètre de périmètre avec 300 mètres de diamètre ; ainsi que l’ensemble des aménagements et équipements nécessaires au fonctionnement de cette première tranche. Cette première phase représente à elle seule un ensemble immobilier important qui constituera le premier noyau opérationnel de la future cité ministérielle. Sa durée prévisionnelle de réalisation est de 24 mois. La seconde phase viendra compléter cet ensemble avec une durée globale prévisionnelle pour les deux phases de 36 mois. La signature de la convention de financement de ce projet est intervenue le 17 décembre 2025 dernier. ATOP/AR/SED/BV

items.title: Education Minister warns AI could breed lazy learners, calls for digital education policy
items.description: The Minister for Education, Haruna Iddrisu, has cautioned against the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) in schools, warning that excessive dependence on the technology could encourage intellectual laziness among learners and undermine their ability to think independently. He acknowledged that artificial intelligence offers significant opportunities to transform teaching and learning but stressed that its adoption must be guided by measures that promote creativity, critical thinking and problem-solving. The Minister maintained that technology should complement the work of teachers and improve the quality of education rather than become a shortcut that prevents students from developing essential academic and intellectual skills. Addressing participants at the 2026 National Education Week and Evidence Summit in Accra, Mr Iddrisu said the government was committed to harnessing technology to improve educational outcomes, but would not support an approach that undermined the role of teachers in the classroom. He warned that the growing use of AI across educational institutions, from primary schools to universities, required careful attention to ensure that students did not become overly dependent on digital tools to complete their academic work. “We need to guard against the use of AI in producing lazy learners from primary school up to the university. It may provide a shortcut which may not provide for the production of quality graduates for our purposes as a country,” he stated. Minister raises concerns over AI dependence Mr Iddrisu’s concerns centre on the possibility that learners could increasingly rely on artificial intelligence to complete assignments, conduct research and generate answers without adequately engaging with the learning process. He argued that while such tools may offer convenience, their inappropriate use could undermine the development of independent thinking and the ability to analyse and solve problems. The Minister’s position is that students must remain actively involved in their education, using technology to strengthen their understanding rather than allowing it to replace the intellectual effort required for meaningful learning. He stressed that the benefits of AI would only be fully realised if its application supported the development of knowledgeable, creative and analytical graduates capable of addressing Ghana’s development needs.

items.title: Expired food seized in South Darfur capital inspection
items.description: Authorities in Nyala, capital of South Darfur, have seized quantities of expired food products during a campaign to inspect markets and shops. The operation aims to protect consumers and prevent the sale of goods that fail to meet health and safety standards. Nyala Municipality in South Darfur has seized quantities of expired food products during an inspection campaign targeting markets and commercial shops, aimed at protecting consumers and preventing the circulation of goods that do not meet health requirements. The municipality’s media office quoted Huda Hamed, director of health at Nyala Municipality, as saying that the seized products included peanuts, juices, flour, tomato paste, and instant noodles, as well as flavoured soft drinks. She confirmed that inspection operations would continue to ensure the safety of food products sold in local markets. The campaign was launched by Musa El Sheikh Taha, secretary-general of the South Darfur state government, who stressed the need to strengthen health inspections of markets and traders and conduct regular campaigns. He said there would be no tolerance of violations that threatened public health. The municipality urged residents to check production and expiry dates and ensure that packaging was intact when purchasing food products. It also called on consumers to report goods that fail to meet the required standards.
