items.title: Ghana secures 6.5m forest carbon credits with potential US$68m value
items.description: Ghana could generate nearly US$68 million from the sale of forest carbon credits after securing international verification for its efforts to reduce deforestation and forest degradation. The country has obtained approximately 6.5 million credits under the Architecture for REDD+ Transactions (ART), becoming the first African country and the third globally, after Guyana and Costa Rica, to achieve the milestone under the REDD+ Environmental Excellence Standard (TREES). Chief Executive of the Forestry Commission, Dr Hugh Brown, says buyers, including participants in the LEAF Coalition, have committed to purchasing four million credits valued at approximately US$43 million. The remaining 2.5 million credits are available for further transactions and could generate an additional US$25 million. However, the Forestry Commission says Ghana is yet to receive the corresponding revenue, stressing that the issuance of verified credits should not be confused with actual payment. “It is important to distinguish credit issuance from receipt of funds. Ghana has secured the verified credits, but yet to receive the corresponding revenues,” Dr Brown said. The credits represent verified reductions in greenhouse gas emissions achieved between 2017 and 2021 through measures to prevent deforestation and forest degradation and restore forest landscapes. Each credit represents one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent in verified emission reductions. Dr Brown said the credits were earned through measurable conservation results and an independent verification process, rather than simply allocated to the country. “These credits were not simply allocated to Ghana. They were earned through results that had to be achieved, measured, reported, independently validated, and verified,” he said. A key component of the programme is its benefit-sharing arrangement, which allocates the largest proportion of potential revenue to forest-fringe communities, farmers and traditional authorities. Under the approved arrangement, these groups are expected to receive 46 per cent of the proceeds. Government institutions, including the Forestry Commission, Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies, COCOBOD and the Ghana National Fire Service, have been allocated 39 per cent. Environmental non-governmental organisations will receive two per cent, while the private sector is allocated three per cent. The remaining 10 per cent will go towards programme management, including verification and validation costs. Dr Brown said the arrangement recognises the role played by local communities and farmers in protecting Ghana’s forests. “Farmers, forest range communities, and traditional authorities contributed directly to this achievement, and have a legitimate interest in how the benefits are shared,” he said. He added that the government was committed to ensuring that the proceeds were distributed transparently and equitably. “It is expected that with these benefits, rural communities will be incentivized to support forest conservation efforts while providing additional resources to government for forest protection and forest landscape restoration interventions,” he said. Ghana’s experience under the Cocoa Forest REDD+ Programme offers an example of how climate finance can support conservation and community development. Between 2023 and 2024, the country received approximately US$21.8 million under the programme. According to Dr Brown, the funding supported forest protection and landscape restoration, alongside the provision of farming inputs, boreholes, health facilities, school blocks and furniture. The latest issuance follows nearly two decades of work, with Ghana beginning its REDD+ journey in 2008. Minister of Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah Kofi, described the development as a historic achievement resulting from successive governments’ efforts to protect the country’s forests. “This is not an achievement that was achieved within a short period. We’ve taken this journey since 2008,” the Minister said. He acknowledged the contributions of successive governments and the Forestry Commission, despite persistent challenges, including illegal logging and illegal mining. “Even in the face of working on all the challenges we face, whether it’s illegal logging, illegal mining, this result is pointing that we are doing the right thing,” he said. The Forestry Commission says the process required investments in forest monitoring, restoration, social and environmental safeguards, benefit-sharing arrangements and institutional capacity. The ART Board approved the issuance on November 10, 2026, following independent verification of Ghana’s forest data, carbon accounting, reported results and compliance with environmental safeguards. Despite the milestone, the Forestry Commission has warned that illegal mining, illegal logging, wildfires and unsustainable agricultural expansion continue to threaten Ghana’s forests and future carbon credit earnings. Dr Brown said the next monitoring phase would cover the period from 2022 to 2026, with any further issuance depending on Ghana demonstrating additional emission reductions, undergoing independent verification and maintaining compliance with the required standards. “Illegal mining, or galamsey, illegal logging, wildfires, and unsustainable agricultural expansion into forest areas continue to threaten forests, water bodies, and potential carbon benefits,” he cautioned. He called for stronger collaboration among government agencies, traditional authorities, farmers and local communities to protect the country’s forest resources. “The issuance of approximately 6.5 million ART TREES credits is not the conclusion of Ghana’s journey, but evidence that our efforts are producing results,” Dr Brown said. He said the immediate priorities were to complete the initial transactions, secure the expected payments, ensure transparent benefit-sharing and obtain appropriate value for the remaining credits.

Ghana’s US$1.5 bn critical minerals plan: Will benefits reach young people, mining communities?
items.description: Government has set ambitious targets for local mineral processing. The real test will be whether the programme creates decent jobs, strengthens Ghanaian businesses and delivers measurable benefits to communities. Ghana’s ambition to move beyond exporting raw minerals has received renewed attention in the 2027 Budget, which proposes a US$1.5 billion investment in critical minerals value addition. The initiative, captured under Pillar Four of the Government’s New Economy programme, seeks to build an industrial minerals economy around gold, manganese, bauxite and lithium. The proposal presents an important opportunity for Ghana to retain more value from its mineral resources. For decades, the country has exported significant quantities of mineral commodities while much of the refining, processing, manufacturing, technology development and skilled employment associated with them have taken place elsewhere. The Government’s plan is therefore built around a clear objective: process more of Ghana’s minerals locally and expand the economic activities that take place beyond extraction. However, the success of this ambition should not be judged only by the volume of minerals processed. It must also be measured by the jobs created, the opportunities available to Ghanaian businesses and the benefits delivered to communities where mining takes place. What the Budget proposes Under Pillar Four, the 2027 Budget proposes an investment of US$1.5 billion to develop an industrial minerals economy centred on manganese, bauxite, lithium and gold. The Budget sets out specific local processing targets. At least 70 per cent of artisanal and small-scale mining (ASM) gold is expected to be refined locally by December 2027. By December 2028, local refining is expected to reach 100 per cent, alongside a prohibition on exports of raw ASM gold. For manganese and bauxite, the Government targets at least 50 per cent local processing by the end of 2028. By the end of 2030, the target is to process all manganese and bauxite locally and prohibit the export of these minerals in their raw form. The Budget also outlines further ambitions for mineral-based industrialisation. Bauxite processing is expected to support alumina refining and aluminium smelting, while lithium development is expected to begin with local refining and progressively advance into battery-grade chemicals, components and cells. These targets represent a significant policy direction. They also establish measurable milestones against which the Government’s progress can be assessed. Infrastructure is central to the ambition The proposed value-addition programme is supported by infrastructure plans intended to connect mineral-producing areas to processing facilities and export markets. The Budget proposes the establishment of a 24-hour critical-minerals processing enclave in the Western Region, with its power backbone to be supported under Pillar Three of the New Economy programme. It also states that construction of the Takoradi–Nyinahin railway line will begin in 2027 using Ghana’s own resources. The proposed route will pass through major mineral towns, including Nsuta and Awaso, and is intended to transport manganese and bauxite to the Western Region processing enclave. The railway plan also includes an extension from Nyinahin to Hamile from 2030. In addition, the Government intends to develop Takoradi Port as a principal maritime gateway to the Sahel, supported by an inland port at Hamile to serve Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger and the wider Sahel region. If implemented effectively, these infrastructure investments could improve the movement of minerals, support industrial activity and strengthen Ghana’s position as a regional processing and trade hub. However, the economic benefits will depend on timely delivery, reliable energy supply, effective coordination and the ability of local industries to make productive use of the infrastructure. The jobs question: What opportunities will young Ghanaians gain? One of the most important tests of the programme will be its contribution to employment, particularly for young people. The Budget identifies skilled jobs as one of the indicators for measuring the success of the critical-minerals programme. The railway is also presented as infrastructure that will support industry, local processing and job creation. This is encouraging, but the Budget’s minerals section does not provide a numerical target for youth employment. It does not specify how many young Ghanaians are expected to be trained, recruited or retained across the proposed processing facilities and related industries. Local processing can create employment beyond mining itself. Opportunities may emerge in mineral processing, engineering, laboratory services, plant operations, equipment maintenance, logistics, environmental management and manufacturing. Yet these opportunities will not automatically translate into employment for young Ghanaians unless the necessary skills, training pathways and recruitment arrangements are deliberately developed. Government should therefore provide a clear skills and employment plan linked to the programme. This should identify the technical skills required, the training institutions expected to contribute, the number of people to be trained and the employment opportunities available to graduates and skilled workers. Without such information, it will be difficult for young people, training institutions and the public to assess whether the programme is translating industrial ambitions into accessible employment opportunities. Will Ghanaian businesses participate meaningfully? Another important measure of success is the extent to which Ghanaian businesses participate in the new mineral value chain. The Budget identifies Ghanaian suppliers as one of the indicators against which the programme’s performance will be measured. This is important because local processing should create opportunities not only for large investors but also for domestic enterprises that can provide goods and services to the industry. These opportunities could include engineering services, fabrication, equipment maintenance, transport, catering, construction, laboratory services and other technical and professional support. However, identifying Ghanaian suppliers as a success indicator is not the same as setting out specific participation targets. The minerals section does not provide a numerical target for local procurement or explain what proportion of contracts is expected to go to Ghanaian-owned businesses. The Government should publish clear local participation measures, including procurement targets, supplier development arrangements and transparent reporting on contracts awarded to Ghanaian enterprises. Such measures would help ensure that the programme strengthens domestic businesses instead of concentrating its benefits among a limited number of large investors. Women and mining communities must not be left behind The programme also raises important questions about inclusion. Women participate in Ghana’s mining economy in different capacities, including mineral trading, processing, services and small-scale mining-related activities. As the sector moves towards more formalised and technology-driven operations, there is a need to ensure that women can access relevant training, employment, business opportunities and leadership positions. The Budget’s minerals section does not set out specific employment or procurement targets for women. It is therefore important for the implementing institutions to clarify how women will participate in the new value chain and what measures will support their inclusion. Mining communities must also be central to the programme’s development. Communities that host mineral extraction and processing activities should be able to identify tangible improvements in their livelihoods, infrastructure and local economic opportunities. The Budget identifies environmental performance as one of the measures of success. However, the minerals section does not provide detailed community benefit-sharing arrangements, compensation frameworks or specific environmental monitoring targets and enforcement measures. These issues should be addressed through transparent implementation plans. Local employment opportunities, community consultation, environmental monitoring, rehabilitation obligations and accessible grievance mechanisms should form part of the programme’s accountability framework. Industrial development should not come at the expense of the communities and natural resources that make it possible. Financing and implementation require close scrutiny The proposed US$1.5 billion investment is a major commitment, but the public will need more information on how it will be financed and deployed. The minerals section of the Budget does not provide a detailed breakdown of the US$1.5 billion across the four minerals, processing facilities, railway infrastructure and other related investments. It is therefore important that Government publishes the project-level allocations, financing arrangements, implementation timelines and responsible institutions. It is also necessary to distinguish the US$1.5 billion critical-minerals investment from the wider New Economy programme. The Budget outlines a US$10 billion investment programme over 2027–2030 and states that GH¢30 billion, equivalent to 1.5 per cent of GDP, will be invested in the New Economy in 2027. These are separate figures and should not be treated as interchangeable. The scale of the proposed programme makes transparency and value-for-money assessment essential. Government must demonstrate how public resources will be used, what investments are expected from private-sector partners and how progress will be reported. The railway, processing enclave and associated infrastructure will also require careful coordination. Delays in power supply, transport infrastructure, financing or industrial investment

items.title: La Bourse de Casablanca finit sur une note négative
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a fini sur une note négative lundi, son indice principal, le MASI, perdant 0,54% à 16.882,6 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a reculé de 0,95% à 1.255,72 pts et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody's ESG Solutions, a cédé 0,17% à 1.268,82 pts. Le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a abandonné 0,6% à 1.594,82 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Assurances » (-4,24%), « Industrie agricole » (-4,06%) et « Ingénieries et biens d'équipement industriels » (-2,99%) ont accusé les plus fortes baisses. À l'inverse, les secteurs « Mines » (+3,77%), « Industrie pharmaceutique » (+1,1%) et « Électricité » (+0,54%) ont signé les meilleures performances. Les échanges ont dépassé 245,4 millions de dirhams (MDH), réalisés principalement sur le marché central « Actions » et dominés par les transactions sur Attijariwafa bank (117,8 MDH), Addoha (40,25 MDH) et Managem (24,24 MDH). La capitalisation boursière s'est établie à plus de 980 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, Wafa Assurance (-7,82% à 5.070 DH), CMGP Group (-4,06% à 260 DH), Stroc Industrie (-3,71% à 149,05 DH), Vicenne (-3,48% à 304 DH) et CFG Bank (-3,43% à 197 DH) ont enregistré les plus fortes baisses. À l'opposé, Jet Energy (+5,27% à 215,8 DH), Minière Touissit (+4,83% à 3.449 DH), S2M (+4,12% à 480 DH), Managem (+3,75% à 1.245 DH) et Lesieur Cristal (+3,69% à 279,95 DH) ont affiché les plus fortes progressions. items.title: PM Shehbaz vows no cap on homes for poor, sets Rs1,000bn disbursement target under Apna Ghar scheme
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday set a target of Rs1,000 billion in disbursements under the Prime Minister Apna Ghar Programme over the next six months. He declared that there was no limit on the number of homes the government would build for the poor, vowing to construct millions if needed. Addressing a ceremony held to mark the milestone of over Rs100bn in loans reaching citizens under the scheme, PM Shehbaz said it was a matter of deep concern that while a few enjoy every comfort, a vast number of people are deprived of shelter, education, healthcare and dignified employment. This, he said, was not the Pakistan envisioned by Quaid-i-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah. The premier said that housing schemes in the past had mostly served the elite, who did not need bank loans, while the real need was among labourers, widows, orphans and low-income families across Pakistan, including Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan. “If the state cannot provide even a roof to such families, it has no right to rule.” The prime minister recalled that the programme was launched in April 2026. “In about six and a half months, banks have disbursed Rs112bn against loan sanctions of about Rs500 billion,” PM Shehbaz said, calling this a good start. However, he maintained that the journey ahead is long and must be covered at “lightning speed”. He directed the finance and housing ministers, the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) governor, and banks to aim for Rs1,000bn in disbursements in the next six months. “Any hurdles and legal impediments will be removed jointly, without exposing banks to undue risk,” he assured the banks. The premier noted that banks had initially been reluctant to enter this segment because of comfortable returns on treasury bills and government deposits. He praised those that came forward and said he was told the scheme was free of corruption and nepotism. The ceremony also featured the presentation of awards to the top five high-performing banks: United Bank Limited Deputy CEO Abdul Aleem Qureshi, Habib Bank Limited President Muhammad Nassir Salim, Bank Alfalah President Atif Bajwa, Meezan Bank Retail Acting CEO/COO Ziaul Hasan, and Mobilink Microfinance Bank Chief Business Officer Attaur Rehman. Announcing recognition for the top five high-performing banks, he said its leaders would be given blue passports, with a notification to be issued the same day. He said it would be for each bank’s owners or CEOs to decide who would hold them. He added that the recognition also carries responsibility, as any delay in genuine loan approvals would now be attributed to them. “An unencumbered and clear title property is the main requirement for a loan, and that other documentation should be handled by banks by helping applicants rather than turning them away,” the prime minister stated. He said some banks had claimed to be unaware of the scheme, which he described as unacceptable, and urged them to set up dedicated cells. Responding to the suggestions of the Association of Builders and Developers (Abad) chairman, PM Shehbaz said he welcomed a proposed tripartite coordination involving Abad, the SBP governor, the builders and banks, and directed the finance minister to hold a meeting with the housing minister and housing secretary. “We want results,” he said, adding he was ready to support the effort if it truly helped build homes. He thanked Housing and Works Minister Riaz Hussain Pirzada, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, Economic Affairs Minister Ahad Khan Cheema, and SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad for their efforts, and appreciated Information Minister Attaullah Tarar for the publicity. Abad Chairman Hanif Kohari appreciated the prime minister for turning the housing initiative into a practical programme, and said it had created opportunities for the construction sector. “Abad, representing about 1,500 members nationwide, is working with the government and banks,” Kohari said. He expressed confidence that the target of 500,000 homes would be met through continued cooperation. The programme beneficiaries also shared their experiences, including Musarrat Qamar (AJK), Dr Asad Ali (Quetta), Anam Akhtar (Rawalpindi), Jameela Bibi (Rahim Yar Khan), and Karachi couple Babar Zaib and Tayyaba Qazi, along with others from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. They said the financing helped them complete or buy homes after years in rented accommodation.

items.title: Ghana Medical Trust Fund moves Miguel to Euracare after Korle Bu’s GH¢77,561 ‘no bed’ delay
items.description: The Ghana Medical Trust Fund has taken over the case of five-year-old Miguel Ntsiful and referred him to Euracare Multi-Specialist Hospital after Korle Bu Teaching Hospital failed to secure an intensive care bed for his brain tumour surgery, despite receiving GH¢77,561 more than two months ago. Miguel, accompanied by his mother, Joyce Donkoh, met neurosurgeon Dr. Jimmy Abubakar at Euracare on Monday, November 23, 2026, following arrangements initiated by the Fund on Friday. The consultation marks a significant step towards securing treatment for the five-year-old, whose surgery has been delayed for three months despite repeated appeals by his mother. Dr. Abubakar reviewed Miguel’s medical history and previous brain scans before requesting a fresh Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scan with and without contrast to assess the tumour and guide further treatment. Read also: Korle Bu sends five-year-old Miguel home for further tests, schedules review for November 24 Miguel is scheduled to undergo the scan on Tuesday, November 24, before returning to Euracare on Thursday for a review and discussions on a possible surgery date. Medical Trust Fund intervenes The intervention follows a series of JoyNews reports highlighting Miguel’s prolonged wait for surgery at Korle Bu and his mother’s desperate appeals for urgent treatment. The Ghana Medical Trust Fund contacted JoyNews following the reports and initiated arrangements for Miguel to receive urgent medical attention at Euracare. The Fund has committed to covering the cost of his treatment. According to the fund, the immediate priority is to save Miguel’s life rather than delay his treatment over the recovery of the money. Following discussions with the Fund’s management, JoyNews Aid of the JoyNews Impact Makers Foundation, which spearheaded the public fundraising campaign, agreed to hand over Miguel’s case to the Fund to facilitate his treatment. The Ghana Medical Trust Fund, also known as MahamaCares, was established under the Ghana Medical Trust Fund Act, 2025 (Act 1144), to provide financial support for Ghanaians suffering from serious and costly chronic illnesses, including cancer, kidney disease and cardiovascular conditions. Introduced by President John Dramani Mahama, the Fund seeks to bridge gaps in the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), which does not fully cover some expensive specialised treatments, leaving many patients and their families struggling to afford life-saving medical care. GH¢77,561 paid, but no surgery at Korle Bu Teaching Hospital Miguel was diagnosed with a posterior fossa brain tumour and obstructive hydrocephalus, a condition that causes excess fluid to accumulate in the brain. He initially underwent surgery at the Cape Coast Teaching Hospital to relieve the fluid build-up but was subsequently referred to Korle Bu Teaching Hospital for the more complex operation to remove the tumour. Following a JoyNews appeal, members of the public contributed towards his treatment, with The Multimedia Group Limited paying the full amount into Korle Bu’s account on September 14, 2026. But more than two months after the payment, the hospital had yet to perform the operation, citing the unavailability of a paediatric intensive care bed. Miguel’s mother, who lives in Gomoa in the Central Region, made several journeys to Korle Bu in Accra, hoping to secure a surgery date for her son. Her desperation was captured in a JoyNews report in which she knelt and pleaded with hospital authorities to find a bed for Miguel. Following the report, Korle Bu announced arrangements for his admission. However, when his mother took him to the hospital on November 18, doctors requested further medical investigations and sent him home. He was asked to return on November 24 after completing the investigations, leaving the family without a definite surgery date. Korle Bu’s Board Chairman, Professor Titus Beyuo, subsequently explained that all eight paediatric intensive care ventilators were occupied, making it unsafe to undertake Miguel’s surgery without guaranteed postoperative intensive care. The hospital also cited administrative challenges in processing the payment made for his treatment. New hope for Miguel The Ghana Medical Trust Fund’s intervention now offers Miguel another opportunity to undergo the operation his mother has spent months seeking. For Miguel’s mother, the hope is that the new arrangement will finally deliver what more than two months of waiting at Korle Bu could not – a definite surgery date for her five-year-old son.

items.title: Koudougou : Le chef du quartier Bourkina destitué pour « défaut d’allégeance et manquements aux usages coutumiers »
items.description: Sa Majesté le Lallé Naaba Guigmdé a destitué Naaba Baongho, chef du quartier Bourkina de Koudougou, pour défaut d'allégeance et manquements aux usages coutumiers », a annoncé lundi la cour royale du Lallé, qui lui reproche notamment son attitude lors de l'ouverture des Nuits atypiques de Koudougou (NAK), samedi 21 novembre 2026. Ces motifs ont été exposés au cours d'un point de presse tenu au palais par plusieurs dignitaires de la cour, notamment le prince Sidiki Kaboré, le Ouid-Nabiga Mathias Ouédraogo, le Ouidi-Naaba Baongo, le Tensoaba Bilga et le Malgré Naaba Tanga. Leurs interventions ont été restituées en français par Barthélemy Gamsonré, également membre de la cour royale. Selon ce dernier, le destitué aurait progressivement cessé de fréquenter le palais royal à partir de 2012. Il lui est en outre reproché de ne pas avoir accompli les démarches coutumières d'allégeance auprès du Lallé Naaba Guigmdé, intronisé en 2021. Barthélemy Gamsonré a aussi évoqué des comportements jugés contraires aux usages coutumiers lors de certaines cérémonies dans le quartier Bourkina. Il a notamment indiqué que l'ancien chef aurait tenu des propos désobligeants à l'endroit d'émissaires du Lallé Naaba. Selon la cour royale, l'incident survenu lors de l'ouverture des NAK a été déterminant. Au passage du Lallé Naaba sur le site du festival, Édouard Yaméogo ne se serait pas conformé aux marques de respect coutumier observées par les autres chefs présents et n'aurait pas manifesté publiquement son allégeance à l'autorité coutumière. Au regard de ces griefs, le Lallé Naaba Guigmdé a décidé de lui retirer son titre de chef de quartier. Selon la cour, la mesure s'étend aux dignitaires qu'il avait lui-même intronisés à ses côtés. Barthélemy Gamsonré a précisé que la procédure coutumière avait été engagée la veille, dimanche 22 novembre, avec la participation des chefs de terre des cinq grands quartiers de Koudougou. La cour royale entend informer les autorités administratives de cette décision afin que les dispositions nécessaires soient prises. Source : Agence d'information du Burkina.

items.title: Bakary Sarr : « Les pouvoirs publics doivent contribuer à créer les conditions d’un exercice libre et responsable du journalisme »
items.description: Les pouvoirs publics doivent contribuer à créer les conditions d'un exercice libre et responsable du journalisme. C’est l’appel lancé lundi, par le ministre de la Communication, Bakary Sarr,lors de la cérémonie d’ouverture de la 1ère édition de la Conférence africaine des jeunes journalistes (CAJJ 2026). Dakar accueille la première édition de la Conférence africaine des jeunes journalistes (CAJJ 2026) du 23 au 24 novembre 2026. Pour cette année, les jeunes reporters des différents pays de l’Afrique vont échanger autour du thème : « Désinformation, discours de haine et droit à l’information : comprendre pour agir en faveur de l’État de droit ». Ayant présidé la cérémonie d’ouverture, le ministre de la Communication, Bakary Sarr a souligné qu’il serait injuste de faire peser sur les seuls journalistes la responsabilité de la qualité de l'espace informationnel. « Les pouvoirs publics doivent contribuer à créer les conditions d'un exercice libre et responsable du journalisme. Les entreprises de presse doivent pouvoir rechercher des modèles économiques viables, sans renoncer à leur indépendance éditoriale. Les citoyens, enfin, doivent être encouragés à développer leur esprit critique et leur capacité à évaluer les informations qu'ils reçoivent », a-t-il dit. A lire aussi : Journalisme africain : Dakar au cœur du débat sur le financement des médias indépendants Car, il estime que l'État de droit ne se construit pas uniquement dans les institutions judiciaires ou les assemblées. Il se nourrit aussi d'un espace public où les citoyens peuvent accéder à une information fiable, confronter librement leurs idées et demander des comptes à ceux qui exercent le pouvoir. Ainsi, au-delà des panels et des ateliers prévus au cours de ces trois journées, cette conférence offre, selon le ministre, « une occasion précieuse » de construire des solidarités professionnelles durables entre jeunes journalistes africains. Pour le ministre, la perspective de mettre en place un réseau ouest-africain des jeunes journalistes constitue, à cet égard, une initiative encourageante. Un tel cadre pourrait favoriser le partage d'expériences, les productions journalistiques collaboratives, les formations communes et les initiatives transfrontalières de vérification de l'information. « L'Appel de Dakar, qui sera élaboré au terme de vos travaux, devra traduire cette volonté en recommandations concrètes. Il importe que les réflexions engagées ici ne restent pas de simples déclarations de principe, mais qu'elles ouvrent la voie à des actions réalisables et à des engagements suivis », a-t-il ajouté. Plaidoyer pour un journalisme africain plus fort, plus solidaire, plus innovant Pour sa part, le président de la Convention des jeunes reporters du Sénégal (Cjrs), Mamadou Diagne, a aussi reconnu que le journalisme africain traverse une période de profondes mutations. Sur ce, il trouve que leurs expériences, leurs innovations, leurs initiatives et leurs réussites doivent circuler au-delà de leurs frontières. « C’est pourquoi nous devons faire de cette rencontre un véritable espace de coopération, et non simplement une succession de panels. Nous devons repartir de Dakar avec des idées, mais aussi avec des engagements, avec des projets, avec des collaborations, avec une volonté commune de construire un journalisme africain plus fort, plus solidaire, plus innovant et davantage connecté aux réalités de nos populations », a-t-il plaidé. D’ailleurs, Mamadou Diagne affirme que la solidarité entre journalistes ne doit pas être un simple slogan prononcé lors de nos rencontres. Elle doit être une exigence, une responsabilité et un engagement collectif. « Cette conférence doit aussi être un espace où nous affirmons notre attachement à la liberté de la presse, à la protection des journalistes et au respect de leurs droits fondamentaux », a-t-il lancé. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Équipe d’Algérie : Brahim Hemdani sur le départ, la FAF tranchera la semaine prochaine
items.description: La mission de Brahim Hemdani et Antar Yahia à la tête de l'équipe d'Algérie de football est pratiquement terminée. À moins d’un rebondissement, le duo ne sera pas sur le banc des Fennecs lors du prochain rassemblement en mars prochain. Toutefois, aucune décision n’a été prise par la Fédération algérienne de football (FAF) le concernant, a-t-on appris de source sûre ce lundi 23 novembre. Le coach des Fennecs et son adjoint Antar Yahia ont présenté dimanche au président de la FAF Walid Sadi leur rapport sur la lourde défaite face au Togo (0-3) en éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, mardi 17 novembre. Selon nos sources, le successeur de Petković s’est plaint de l’atmosphère qui règne autour de l’équipe nationale et fait part au patron de la FAF des difficultés à poursuivre sa mission. « Brahim Hemdani pense qu’il ne peut pas tenir avec cette pression exagérée et démesurée autour de l’équipe nationale. Son retour à la Direction technique nationale est fort possible », explique notre source en précisant qu’« aucune décision n’a été prise avant la réunion du Bureau fédéral la semaine prochaine ». Le président de la FAF a signifié sa fin de mission au staff technique Le quotidien algérien spécialisé Compétition a indiqué que le président de la FAF a décidé de se séparer de Brahim Hemdani. Les deux anciens internationaux ont été chargés de la mission de conduire la barre technique des Verts en septembre dernier, avec l'approche des éliminatoires de la CAN et l'échec des négociations engagées avec des entraîneurs étrangers de renom. Hemdani et Antar Yahia : Bilan mitigé et énorme pression Brahim Hemdani venait de réaliser un exploit avec les U21 qu’il a menés à la victoire finale aux Jeux méditerranéens en août dernier, en Italie. Saïb Moussa a, lui, été nommé manager général de l’équipe. Le bilan du staff technique avec l'équipe nationale est mitigé. En cinq matchs, les Verts ont réalisé trois victoires, dont deux en éliminatoires de la CAN (contre la Zambie 3-1 et le Togo 1-0) et une en amical face au Niger (2-1). L'équipe a aussi été tenue en échec au Burundi (2-2) et sévèrement battue au Togo (3-0). C'est ce score inattendu qui a changé la donne et a amené la fédération à demander des comptes à Hemdani, dont une partie de la presse et du public réclame la même chose à cause des prestations peu convaincantes de l’équipe même lorsqu’elle gagnait. Le staff technique de l’Algérie n’a pas eu la tâche facile La FAF pourrait se séparer de ce duo bien que celui-ci ait à sa décharge le nombre record de joueurs blessés simultanément. Face au Togo, il a joué sans huit des joueurs habituellement titulaires, dont Ibrahim Maza et Bachir Belloumi. Il faut dire que Hemdani et Yahia n’ont pas eu la tâche facile. Sur le plan comptable aussi, le bilan n'est pas catastrophique. L’objectif fixé à Brahim Hemdani est de qualifier l'équipe à la Coupe d'Afrique des nations 2027. Après quatre journées et à deux matchs de la fin des éliminatoires, les Verts sont leaders de leur groupe avec 7 points. Il leur suffit d’une victoire pour être assurés d'être présents au tournoi final. L’article Équipe d'Algérie : Brahim Hemdani sur le départ, la FAF tranchera la semaine prochaine est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: UPSA’s FAF Awards to honour The Multimedia Group CEO Kwasi Twum
items.description: Founder of the Multimedia Group, Kwasi Twum, is set to be honoured at the 2026 edition of the Faculty of Accounting and Finance (FAF) Eminent Achievement Awards at the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA). The recognition celebrates his contribution to Ghana’s media industry, particularly his role in building Joy FM and its sister platforms into one of the country’s influential radio stations and establishing the Multimedia Group as a major player in broadcasting and digital media. The awards ceremony is scheduled for Friday, November 27, at 4:00 p.m. at the UPSA Auditorium. In announcing the recognition, organisers highlighted Mr Twum’s journey from establishing Joy FM in 1995 to building a multimedia organisation that has contributed to national discourse and created opportunities for generations of media professionals. His legacy, they noted, extends beyond radio, television and digital platforms to include institution-building, public accountability and the strengthening of democratic participation. The 2026 awards are being held under the theme, “Celebrating Excellence. Honouring Legacies. Inspiring National Transformation.” The FAF Eminent Achievement Awards were instituted by the Faculty of Accounting and Finance at UPSA to recognise individuals whose professional careers have contributed to excellence, innovation and transformation in accounting, finance, banking and economics. The maiden edition was held in November 2025 under the theme, “Recognising Trailblazers: Driving Excellence and Transformation in Accounting, Finance and Economics.” At the inaugural ceremony, four industry leaders – Naa Alhassan Andani, Winfred Kwasi Dodzih, Frank Brako Adu Jr and Edward Effah — were recognised for their contributions to their respective fields. Two institutions, Abokobi Area Rural Bank and Juaben Rural Bank, also received special honours. The award scheme seeks to celebrate leaders whose work has strengthened institutions, advanced professional practice and inspired younger generations. It also forms part of the Faculty’s efforts to bridge the gap between academia and industry through recognition, dialogue, mentorship and collaboration.

items.title: Siguiri : douze femmes condamnées à un an de prison avec sursis pour exploitation illégale de l’or
items.description: ‎Le tribunal de première instance de Siguiri a rendu, ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, son verdict dans une affaire d’exploitation illégale de l’or et de dégradation de l’environnement impliquant douze femmes. Toutes ont été reconnues coupables des faits qui leur étaient reprochés. ‎ ‎À l’issue de l’audience correctionnelle, présidée par Boubacar III Barry, le tribunal a déclaré les douze prévenues coupables des délits d’exploitation illégale de mines d’or et de destruction de l’environnement. ‎ ‎En répression, chacune des condamnées a écopé d’un an d’emprisonnement, assorti du sursis, ainsi que d’une amende de trois millions de francs guinéens. Le montant total des amendes s’élève ainsi à 36 millions de francs guinéens. Les frais de justice ont également été mis à leur charge. ‎ ‎Lors de ses réquisitions, le ministère public, représenté par Mohamed Samoura et Simon Pierre Millimono, avait requis deux ans d’emprisonnement et trois millions de francs guinéens d’amende contre chacune des prévenues. ‎ ‎Ce verdict s’inscrit dans un contexte de renforcement de la lutte contre l’exploitation minière illégale et la dégradation de l’environnement dans la région de Siguiri, où l’orpaillage clandestin demeure une préoccupation majeure.

items.title: 33 660 orpailleurs enrôlés dans le processus de formalisation
items.description: Le ministre des Mines et de la Géologie, Cheikhou Oumar Seck, a présidé, ce lundi 23 novembre 2026, à Bakel, un Comité départemental de développement (CDD) consacré à la formalisation de l’exploitation minière artisanale. À cette occasion, il a fait le point sur les avancées du programme national, annoncé la mise en place de six couloirs pilotes et évoqué la création d’un comptoir national de commercialisation de l’or. La formalisation de l’exploitation minière artisanale franchit une nouvelle étape dans les régions de Tambacounda et de Kédougou. En déplacement à Bakel, ce lundi 23 novembre, le ministre des Mines et de la Géologie, Cheikhou Oumar Seck, a annoncé que 33 660 orpailleurs ont déjà été enrôlés dans le cadre du processus d’identification biométrique. Parmi eux, 6 837 sont recensés dans la région de Tambacounda, contre 26 823 à Kédougou. Ces chiffres ont été communiqués lors d’un Comité départemental de développement organisé dans le cadre du Programme national de formalisation de l’exploitation minière artisanale, en prélude à la tournée économique du président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Diakhar Faye. Pour le ministre, cette opération constitue un levier essentiel pour mieux encadrer un secteur qui fait vivre de nombreuses familles et représente une source importante de revenus pour les jeunes et les femmes. Il reconnaît toutefois que l’exploitation informelle expose les territoires à de multiples risques, notamment les accidents, les trafics illicites, la pollution des eaux, la dégradation des sols et les pertes de recettes publiques. « La formalisation n’est donc pas une sanction. Elle est une protection », a-t-il soutenu, estimant que cette démarche doit permettre aux orpailleurs d'obtenir un statut reconnu, d'accéder à des espaces légalement définis et de bénéficier de meilleures conditions de sécurité et d'accompagnement. Six couloirs pilotes en cours d'aménagement Pour accompagner cette réforme, le ministère des Mines et de la Géologie a signé une convention avec la Caisse des dépôts et consignations (CDC), à travers sa filiale Synapsys Conseils SA. L'accord porte sur la mise en place d'un système d'identification biométrique et la délivrance de cartes sécurisées aux acteurs de l'exploitation minière artisanale. Le dispositif sera complété par une convention interministérielle conclue avec le ministère des Forces armées. Celle-ci vise notamment à sécuriser les sites d'exploitation, à formaliser les activités et à lutter contre les réseaux illicites. À ce titre, six couloirs pilotes sont actuellement en cours d'aménagement et de clôture par le Génie militaire. Les missions techniques effectuées à Bakel, Goudiry, Alinguel et Samba Yaye ont également permis de relever les attentes des populations, mais aussi les difficultés d'accès à certains sites. Le ministre a assuré que ces contraintes seront prises en charge. La Falémé, une priorité environnementale Au-delà de l'organisation du secteur, la préservation de l'environnement figure parmi les priorités affichées par les autorités. Cheikhou Oumar Seck a particulièrement insisté sur la protection de la Falémé, confrontée aux conséquences de certaines pratiques d'exploitation minière. « Les pratiques dangereuses, la pollution des eaux, la dégradation des sols et la coupe abusive du bois ne seront pas tolérées », a-t-il averti. Il a ainsi rappelé que la formalisation doit nécessairement s'accompagner du respect des prescriptions environnementales. Dans cette perspective, le ministre a appelé les artisans miniers à se faire identifier, à s'organiser en groupements d'intérêt économique (GIE) et à respecter les limites des couloirs d'exploitation ainsi que les règles de sécurité. Il a également invité les autorités territoriales, les collectivités locales, les services techniques et les Forces de défense et de sécurité à renforcer leur coordination. Un comptoir national pour mieux valoriser l'or Autre annonce majeure : la mise en place d'un comptoir national de commercialisation de l'or, piloté par la Société des mines du Sénégal (SOMISEN). Ce mécanisme devrait couvrir l'ensemble de la production aurifère, qu'elle soit industrielle, artisanale, semi-mécanisée ou issue de la petite mine. Selon le ministre, le dispositif aura pour missions de maîtriser les flux d'or, de favoriser la valorisation locale de la production, d'approvisionner le marché national et d'accroître les recettes publiques. Son fonctionnement reposera notamment sur l'achat de l'or auprès des producteurs, son affinage et sa commercialisation, avec un dispositif de transport sécurisé vers la raffinerie. La certification de la raffinerie de Diamniadio et le développement de la bijouterie nationale sont également annoncés comme des leviers d'accompagnement. Le montage du projet associera l'État, le Fonds souverain d'investissements stratégiques (FONSIS), les banques et des partenaires commerciaux. « Il s'agit, pour notre pays, de capter la valeur ajoutée de son or, de créer des emplois, de soutenir l'artisanat et la bijouterie nationale et de réduire les circuits frauduleux », a expliqué Cheikhou Oumar Seck. À travers ces différentes mesures, le gouvernement entend faire de la formalisation de l'exploitation minière artisanale un instrument de sécurisation des activités, de préservation des ressources naturelles et de meilleure redistribution des retombées de l'or au profit des populations et de l'économie nationale. A. N

items.title: Importations de bétail : Lekjaa veut en finir avec la logique de la rente
items.description: Le gouvernement entend revoir les mécanismes d’importation du bétail et des viandes, tout en rompant avec les pratiques qu’il assimile à une logique de rente. C’est le message défendu par Fouzi Lekjaa, ministre de l’Économie et des Finances et de l’Efficacité publique, lors de l’examen détaillé du projet de loi de finances (PLF) pour 2027, lundi, devant la commission des finances, de la planification et du développement économique à la Chambre des conseillers. Au cœur des échanges, les exonérations douanières que l’exécutif envisage d’appliquer, à partir du début de l’année prochaine, aux importations d’animaux vivants des espèces bovine, ovine et caprine, ainsi qu’aux viandes et abats qui en sont issus, qu’ils soient frais, réfrigérés ou congelés. Face aux interrogations soulevées autour de ces mesures, Fouzi Lekjaa a défendu une approche fondée sur les réalités du marché. « Le marché de la viande au Maroc ne saurait faire l’objet d’interprétations politiques, mais il est régi par les seuls faits, lesquels doivent départager les différentes orientations », a-t-il déclaré, annonçant la volonté de mettre un terme à la logique des « bons ». Le ministre a notamment reconnu les limites des dispositifs précédemment mis en place. « Les mesures que nous avons prises auparavant, notamment l’aide financière directe accordée aux importateurs pour chaque tête de bétail, n’ont pas été efficaces », a-t-il admis. Une position qu’il affirme avoir déjà exprimée devant les deux chambres du Parlement, aussi bien pendant la campagne électorale qu’en dehors de celle-ci. Pour le responsable gouvernemental, la situation exige une réponse qui ne se limite pas à une mesure isolée. La première étape consiste à faciliter les importations, tout en tenant compte des contraintes du marché international. « Il ne faut pas croire que les marchés étrangers nous attendent et sont prêts à nous vendre leurs produits. Il existe une concurrence mondiale et des besoins croissants dans tous les pays, d’autant plus que les denrées alimentaires sont désormais devenues des produits stratégiques », a-t-il fait valoir. Cette ouverture du marché doit toutefois s'accompagner, selon lui, d'une rupture avec les pratiques de favoritisme. Fouzi Lekjaa a prévenu que si les importations continuaient de fonctionner sur la base du clientélisme, le gouvernement n'aurait d'autre choix que de revoir le dispositif et de rétablir les droits de douane. « La création de nouveaux foyers de rente est inacceptable et ne présente aucun intérêt », a-t-il insisté. Le ministre a également dénoncé les accusations de ceux qui assimilent cette orientation à un retour aux modèles économiques communistes. « Dès lors que vous leur demandez de renoncer à la rente, ils vous accusent de vouloir rétablir le communisme », a-t-il ironisé, en référence aux systèmes des kolkhozes et des sovkhozes . Avant de rappeler que « le libéralisme ne repose-t-il pas, dans son essence même, sur la concurrence, laquelle doit profiter au consommateur ? ». Au-delà de la régulation des importations, Fouzi Lekjaa a mis en avant la nécessité de préserver le cheptel national, menacé par une pression excessive sur les abattages. Selon lui, le recours aux importations constitue un moyen de prévenir son épuisement et d'éviter une diminution durable des effectifs, particulièrement chez les femelles reproductrices. Il a ainsi expliqué que l'abattage d'une seule brebis représente, en pratique, une perte d'une tête et demie de mouton pour l'année suivante, compte tenu du taux de reproduction naturel du cheptel. Certaines brebis donnent naissance à deux agneaux par an, tandis que d'autres n'en mettent au monde qu'un seul. Le ministre a, dans ce contexte, appelé à poursuivre les opérations d'importation en garantissant une transparence totale et un accès à l'ensemble des marchés internationaux. L'État devra exercer un contrôle aussi bien sur les prix à l'importation que sur les prix de vente, sans pour autant empêcher les importateurs de dégager une marge commerciale légitime, comparable à celle pratiquée par les opérateurs dans le reste du monde. Une condition demeure néanmoins essentielle : que l'accès à l'importation soit garanti à tous les opérateurs sur un pied d'égalité. Fouzi Lekjaa a enfin mis en garde contre les conséquences d'une absence de décisions courageuses, estimant que la crise risquerait autrement de s'aggraver. Il a rappelé que les mesures envisagées poursuivent deux objectifs principaux : permettre à l'éleveur marocain (kessab) de préserver sa place et de continuer à développer son cheptel, comme il l'a toujours fait, tout en garantissant au consommateur un accès à la viande à des prix raisonnables, comparables à ceux pratiqués par le passé. Ces explications ont été apportées après les critiques formulées par Ahmed Hmimid, membre du groupe parlementaire istiqlalien à la Chambre des conseillers. Celui-ci a notamment déploré l'absence d'un cadre juridique et de procédures réglementaires suffisamment élaborés pour accompagner les décisions d'exonération douanière. Le conseiller parlementaire a également pointé la responsabilité de l'Office national de sécurité sanitaire des produits alimentaires (ONSSA) et du ministère de l'Agriculture dans la complexification des procédures d'importation. Il leur a reproché de prendre des décisions de manière unilatérale, sans associer les professionnels du secteur ni les chambres d'agriculture à l'élaboration des cahiers des charges. The post Importations de bétail : Lekjaa veut en finir avec la logique de la rente appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Télécommunications dans l’UEMOA : Le Directeur général de Telecel Faso boucle deux ans à la tête de la COFTEL
items.description: La 17e assemblée générale de la Conférence des opérateurs et fournisseurs de services de télécommunications de l’Union économique et monétaire ouest-africaine (COFTEL) s’est ouverte ce 23 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Les travaux sont présidés par le Directeur général de Telecel Faso et président de la COFTEL, Boris Compaoré, en présence des représentants du ministère en charge de la transition digitale et de la Commission de l’UEMOA. Placée sous le thème « Réseaux satellitaires LEO : quels défis pour la souveraineté numérique, l’équité concurrentielle et la pérennité des investissements des opérateurs télécoms dans l’espace UEMOA ? » , cette rencontre vise à permettre aux acteurs du secteur de mieux s’adapter aux évolutions technologiques et aux nouveaux enjeux du numérique. Elle constitue un cadre d’échanges et de réflexion sur les mutations du secteur des télécommunications. Les participants sont notamment invités à réfléchir à de nouvelles stratégies pour améliorer la qualité des services, relever les défis liés au numérique et assurer la croissance durable de leurs activités. Pour le représentant du ministre en charge de la transition digitale, Nongomzanga Zongo, cette rencontre offre une occasion aux acteurs de réfléchir ensemble aux perspectives du secteur. « Celui qui maîtrise ces infrastructures numériques et ces compétences dispose d’un avantage stratégique considérable dans le monde contemporain » , a-t-il affirmé. Le président de la COFTEL, Boris Compaoré, quant à lui, a souligné l’importance des satellites en orbite basse, appelés satellites LEO. Selon lui, cette technologie constitue une innovation majeure qui pourrait contribuer à améliorer la couverture des populations en matière de télécommunications. Pour sa part, le Directeur de cabinet du département chargé du développement de l’entreprise, des mines, de l’énergie et de l’économie numérique de l’UEMOA, Thierry Koamé, a relevé les difficultés persistantes d’accès aux services numériques en Afrique. « En Afrique, 9 % de la population vit hors de la portée des réseaux mobiles haut débit . Parmi les 63 % de la population vivant dans des zones couvertes par les réseaux, une partie importante n’a pas accès à l’internet mobile » , a-t-il indiqué. Après deux années de présidence assurée par le Burkina Faso, le Niger prend la relève à la tête de la COFTEL. Au terme des travaux, les participants sont attendus sur des propositions concrètes pour accompagner la transition digitale, renforcer la souveraineté numérique et favoriser le développement du secteur des télécommunications dans l’espace UEMOA. Grâce KABRE/BAZIE (Stagiaire) Faso7 L’article Télécommunications dans l’UEMOA : Le Directeur général de Telecel Faso boucle deux ans à la tête de la COFTEL est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Peshawar to host opening ceremony, inaugural match for 12th edition of PSL: PCB chief
items.description: PESHAWAR: Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) Chairman Mohsin Naqvi said on Monday that Peshawar will host the opening ceremony and the inaugural match for the 12th edition of the HBL Pakistan Super League (PSL) scheduled for next year. Naqvi made the announcement while addressing a press conference alongside Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi in Peshawar. “The biggest announcement today, for which I congratulate both the governor and Peshawar Zalmi, is that after 12 years, PSL will hold its opening ceremony and first match in Peshawar,” the PCB chief said. He added that multiple matches will be held in the provincial capital, with the schedule to be finalised later by PSL. The 12th edition of the cricket tournament will be held from March 18 to May 2, 2027. The announcement by Naqvi came shortly after Kundi — whose administration now runs the province under governor’s rule — said the name of Arbab Niaz Stadium would be restored, reversing the PTI government’s decision to rename it to Imran Khan Stadium. In its press release, PCB stated: “The announcement marks a defining moment for cricket in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and for the thousands of supporters who have followed the league, and their team, from afar since the very first season in 2016.” The board noted that fans in Peshawar “have filled stands, packed streets and carried their colours across the country for more than a decade, without once watching an HBL PSL match in their own city”. “That changes with HBL PSL 12. Peshawar’s supporters will finally experience the league’s electric atmosphere at home, with the world’s best T20 talent on show in front of a crowd that has earned its moment,” the statement declared. “This is a moment the league, and above all the fans of Peshawar, have been looking forward to for 12 years,” PSL Chief Executive Officer Salman Naseer was quoted as saying. “Peshawar’s love for cricket is unmatched, and HBL PSL 12 will finally give that passion the stage it deserves. Adding a sixth venue is a major step in the growth of the league, and we look forward to delivering a memorable experience for every fan who walks into the stadium.” Speaking to the media, the PCB chairman noted that Peshawar Zalmi and its owner Javed Afridi had also been wishing for the tournament to come to the city. Naqvi, also the interior minister, stated that matters related to law and order in the province were “improving very rapidly”. He recalled that Governor Kundi would call for “reviving cricket in KP” whenever the two met, even before the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in the province on Oct 11. “This province has produced amazing stars for the cricket team, and I strongly believe that with some promotion and streamlining, […] along with joint efforts, we will see positive results from here in months, not years,” the PCB chief said. He also announced holding a week-long cricket tournament between the U-19 team, Pakistan Shaheens and the national team. Peshawar was supposed to host a PSL match on March 28 in the previous edition, but matches were restricted to Karachi and Lahore as part of austerity measures after the US-Iran war broke out. Asked about that, Naqvi maintained that “best efforts” were made so a match could be staged in Peshawar, but it could not happen due to “purely administrative issues and some concerns”. He clarified there was no “political reason” for not holding the match, adding that Peshawar was an option for one of the venues but it was not announced as such. Responding to a query, Naqvi said that there were plans underway to build an academy for tribal districts, with the specifics of its location and construction timeline to be finalised in the next two weeks. “Those districts are also very important for us,” he affirmed. The merged districts are among the 12 districts where special emergency measures were imposed on Oct 11 as the areas were deemed to face intense security challenges. Speaking on district-level cricket grounds, Naqvi said the PCB planned to work in collaboration with the government to maintain grounds at “whatever level possible”. ‘Preserving Peshawar’s history’: Kundi on reversing stadium name change Announcing his administration’s decision to restore Arbab Niaz Stadium’s name, Kundi said on X: “In 13 years, despite KP’s immense sporting talent, the PTI could not build a single new cricket stadium, even though the Pakistan cricket team boasts a significant number of Pathan players. Yet, they were quick to rename the one we already had.” He contended that the decision was about “preserving Peshawar’s history, respecting its heritage and honouring those who have genuinely contributed to the province’s sporting legacy through their work and achievements”. The stadium was named after Arbab Niaz, a former federal minister for sports. In Feb 2025, the PTI government in KP, led by then-chief minister Ali Amin Gandapur, renamed it after PTI founder and ex-premier Imran Khan. Speaking on the matter during Monday’s press conference, Kundi termed the renaming of the stadium as a “huge injustice to the people of Peshawar”. The governor highlighted that Niaz had the cricket ground built in the 1980s, stating that putting one’s plaques on past projects completed by others was inappropriate. “If they had built it themselves and named it after him, that would have been fine,” the PPP leader said, adding that the name would be restored within a few days. Speaking about provincial matters, Kundi reaffirmed that countering terrorism remained the top priority. He stated that 70 per cent of a Rs160 billion package announced by the federal government will be allotted to the 12 designated districts, while the remaining 30 per cent will go to the rest of KP. He also highlighted his administration’s crackdown on encroachments and illegal placer gold mining, and a cleanliness campaign.

items.title: Legal reforms meaningless without access to lawyers – AG
items.description: Attorney-General and Minister for Justice Dr Dominic Ayine says Ghana’s legal reforms will have limited impact if vulnerable people cannot afford legal representation to enforce their rights. He has therefore called for the State to take greater responsibility for legal aid, particularly for individuals who face legal challenges but lack the financial means to secure a lawyer. Speaking at the 2026 International Conference of the African Women Lawyers Association (AWLA), Dr Ayine said access to justice must be treated as an essential part of the country’s law reform efforts. “Legal aid is not an afterthought to law reform. It is part of it,” he said. The Attorney-General said a law protecting the inheritance rights of widows would mean little if those affected did not know about their rights or could not afford to challenge attempts to dispossess them. He said the same concerns applied to women seeking to enforce their property rights following divorce or the death of a spouse. “The best intestate succession law in the world means nothing to a widow who does not know it exists, or who cannot afford to enforce it against a powerful family,” he said. Dr Ayine argued that access to legal representation was necessary to ensure that rights guaranteed under the law could be enjoyed in practice, particularly by people in underserved communities. He drew on his previous work at the Centre for Public Interest Law, where he represented individuals and communities who could not afford legal services. He said his experience, including cases handled at the High Court in Tarkwa, had shown him the difficulties vulnerable people face in accessing justice. According to him, the distance between a legal right written in a statute and one enjoyed by an individual in a community can be significant. He acknowledged the contribution of women lawyers who have supported vulnerable people through pro bono services and community legal clinics. However, he said the State needed to assume a greater share of the responsibility for ensuring that people could access legal representation. His comments formed part of a broader call for collaboration among lawyers, the judiciary, Parliament, government and civil society to make legal reforms effective across Ghana.

items.title: Azerbaijan Further Tightens Grip on Civil Society
items.description: Click to expand Image Azerbaijani rights defender Bashir Suleymanli in Baku, July 23, 2024. © 2024 Vano Shlamov/AFP via Getty Images Azerbaijan’s parliament on November 18 approved sweeping amendments to legislation governing nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) that would expand government powers to suspend and dissolve independent groups, impose new registration requirements, and further restrict their operations. The following day, a court sentenced prominent rights defender Bashir Suleymanli to seven and a half years in prison, the latest in a series of harsh sentences against civil society activists prosecuted over foreign funding. The proposed legislation would allow authorities, rather than courts, to suspend NGOs for up to a year for broadly defined violations, including failure to meet transparency and anti-money laundering requirements. It would also expand grounds for court-ordered dissolution to include activities deemed a threat to the “legally protected interests of the state and society”—vague standards open to abuse. Existing NGOs would have just 30 days after the law takes effect to revise their charters and apply for re-registration. The minimum capital to establish a nonprofit foundation, a type of nongovernmental organization, would increase tenfold, from 10,000 to 100,000 manats (approx. US$ 59,000). Together, these requirements would create additional barriers to establishing and maintaining independent civil society organizations in Azerbaijan. Human Rights Watch has documented how existing restrictions on registration and foreign funding have forced many independent groups to close or severely curtail their activities. The European Court of Human Rights has repeatedly found violations of freedom of association in cases involving Azerbaijani civil society organizations. Authorities took another strike at civil society on November 19 when the Baku Grave Crimes Court convicted Suleymanli, director of the Institute for Citizens’ Rights, of apparent politically motivated charges of money laundering and abuse of office. Arrested in March 2025, authorities prosecuted Suleymanli as part of a reopened investigation into foreign-funded NGO work. Courts have also handed down lengthy prison sentences to other activists prosecuted in connection with the same investigation, including eight years for Asaf Ahmadov and seven years and three months for Zamin Zaki (Zakiyev). Election monitor Anar Mammadli received a 13-year sentence in September following an unfair trial. Azerbaijani authorities should withdraw the proposed amendments, release Suleymanli and other civil society activists imprisoned for their legitimate work, and end the misuse of criminal law against independent groups. Azerbaijan’s international partners should press the government to uphold its obligations to protect freedom of association.

items.title: AG identifies gap between Ghana’s minimum marriage age and age of sexual consent
items.description: Attorney-General and Minister for Justice Dr Dominic Ayine has identified a legal disparity between Ghana’s minimum age of marriage and the age of sexual consent, saying proposed amendments to the country’s child protection laws provide an opportunity to address the issue. He said Ghana’s minimum age of marriage is 18, while the age of sexual consent under the Criminal Code is 16. Dr Ayine warned that the difference creates a legal gap that could be exploited by individuals seeking to take advantage of children. Speaking at the 2026 International Conference of the African Women Lawyers Association (AWLA), he said amendments to the Children’s Act, 1998 (Act 560), and the Juvenile Justice Act, 2003 (Act 653), were at an advanced stage. He said the proposed changes were among the issues Ghana reported to the United Nations Committee on the Rights of the Child when the country appeared before it in Geneva in January 2026. According to the Attorney-General, the amendments are expected to strengthen Ghana’s response to child marriage, child labour in mining and fishing communities, and the online sexual exploitation of children. He said the country had established a strong legal foundation for child protection but needed to update its laws to respond more effectively to emerging challenges. Ghana became the first country in the world to ratify the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child in February 1990. The country has since enacted several laws and signed international agreements aimed at protecting children, including the Children’s Act, the Juvenile Justice Act and the Domestic Violence Act, 2007. It is also a party to the African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child. Dr Ayine urged women lawyers to bring the same advocacy and legal expertise they had applied to inheritance and matrimonial property reforms to the proposed child protection legislation. He said lawyers had an important role to play in ensuring that reforms moved beyond legislative proposals and translated into practical protection for children. He cited examples from South Africa, Kenya and Nigeria, where legislation has been developed to consolidate child protection and strengthen the rights of children. The Attorney-General said Ghana must now advance the proposed amendments to ensure its child protection framework responds adequately to the needs and vulnerabilities of children.

items.title: Cassava Processor innovator wins GH¢300,000 MTN Pitch
items.description: A young social innovator has won the maiden MTN National Business Pitch Competition for using locally made machines to solve cassava waste challenges. Theophilus Aboagye, CEO of Age Industries and Trading Company Limited, beat four other finalists in a keen contest at the Laplam Court in Accra to take home the GH¢300,000 grand prize. The five finalists each made a presentation to justify why they should win, followed by tough questions from the judging panel. Age Industries designs and manufactures agricultural machinery for smallholder farmers and food processors. The company focuses on equipment for processing cassava, palm fruits and cereals. Its innovations seek to reduce post-harvest losses, improve agricultural productivity and increase farmers’ incomes by making locally manufactured processing equipment more accessible and affordable. Organised by MTN Ghana as part of its 30th-anniversary celebrations, the competition attracted hundreds of applications from entrepreneurs across the country. After screening, 48 businesses advanced to the regional auditions, where judges selected one winner from each of Ghana’s 16 regions. The 16 regional finalists then took part in a three-day boot camp in Accra, where they received practical training and mentorship in financial management, corporate governance, digital transformation, marketing and investment readiness. A final evaluation narrowed the field to five contestants. Each of the 16 regional finalists received GH¢30,000, while additional GH¢30,000 awards were given to outstanding businesses in categories including resilience, sustainability and innovation. Beyond the cash prizes, all five finalists will receive 12 months of post-competition support, including quarterly business reviews, coaching and introductions to prospective investors, suppliers and buyers. Speaking at the event, the Chief Enterprise Officer of MTN Ghana, Angela Mensah Poku, congratulated the five finalists. She described their journey as a remarkable achievement and a sign of the strength of small businesses in the country. She said the competition started with a call to businesses across Ghana to share their stories, showcase their ideas and demonstrate what they were capable of achieving. The call received an overwhelming response, with hundreds of applications from across the country. She said behind every business is a dream, a story, a great deal of hard work and often many sacrifices. She said MTN’s commitment to SMEs goes beyond the competition. Before the National Business Pitch, the company had already supported nine businesses with GH¢30,000 each. It has also invested in initiatives such as SME Clinics, business development sessions and other capacity-building programmes to equip entrepreneurs with the knowledge, tools and confidence they need to grow.“For us, it has never been just about giving out money. It is about what that money makes possible,” she said. She explained that the support is meant to help businesses buy new equipment, expand their operations, create employment, reach new markets and contribute more meaningfully to Ghana’s economy. She said MTN’s ambition is to go beyond being a telecommunications provider to becoming a true technology partner to businesses, providing connectivity, digital solutions, tools and support to help them operate more efficiently, reach more customers and compete in an increasingly digital world. She said as MTN celebrates its 30th anniversary, initiatives like the National Business Pitch reflect its commitment to being a force for good in the communities and markets it serves. When businesses grow, she said, communities grow, jobs are created and the entire economy benefits. She thanked the judges, mentors and coaches for lending their expertise, time and experience to the process, and urged the finalists to leave with new business connections, meaningful relationships, fresh perspectives and the inner confidence to keep pushing forward.
